item.title: Makinde scores Tinubu administration 34 per cent
item.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has scored President Bola Tinubu’s administration 34 per cent, saying the government has failed to secure the support of a majority of Nigerians. Makinde gave the assessment during an interview with Arise Television, where he was asked to evaluate the administration’s performance in infrastructure, diplomacy and economic growth. He likened the score to the percentage of Nigerians who supported Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, arguing that the President needed to win over those who voted against him to build a national consensus. “It’s just about the same percentage as the people that supported him in 2023, 34 per cent. You need the 66 per cent of Nigerians that were against him in 2023 to be on board. This is a national project,” he said. The governor also criticised what he described as pressure on elected officials to join the ruling All Progressives Congress, alleging that some governors were compelled to defect. “Look at what we’ve seen. You have the governors come to APC. If you don’t, you’ll be blackmailed,” he said. Makinde, who is seeking the presidency in 2027 under the Action Peoples Party (APM), also addressed whether he would accept defeat if the election was free, fair and credible. Responding to a question on whether he would concede defeat and retire to farming, the governor said he would accept the outcome if the electoral process met the required standards. “There are a few things that must happen. If the process is free, fair, and credible, yes, I will,” he said. However, when asked whether he would remain in the APM after the election, Makinde said his political future would depend on how Nigerians received his political agenda. “I may evaluate my political future depending on how Nigerians, you know, see this agenda,” he added. The post Makinde scores Tinubu administration 34 per cent appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The Outlook - Week 10 (SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN, LAC-BAL)
item.description: Hey, folks! We’re back with our third and final block of games for the Week 10 NFL slate, and we’re covering all three late games, Sunday Night Football and Monday Night Football! We’ve compiled the game groupings here to make it easier to find the games you want: Block 1: WAS-NYG, NE-DET, KC-ATL, HOU-CLE, MIA-IND Block 2: JAC-TEN, MIN-GB, CAR-NO, BUF-NYJ Block 3: SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN, LAC-BAL “The Outlook” will give you the details, stats, analysis, recommendations and everything else you need to make informed fantasy football decisions. Every fantasy-relevant player on each team will be profiled in this article. We want everyone reading this to bring home championships in their fantasy leagues! I’m incredibly excited to bring this article to all of you this season, and I hope you enjoy the ride. If you have any questions, feel free to find me on Bluesky (@ktompkinsii.bsky.social) or tag me in a post with any lineup questions. I’ll do my best to answer them for you. Let’s get into it! All game and implied point totals listed were compiled via DraftKings Sportsbook on Thursday for SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN and LAC-BAL. Teams on bye in Week 9: Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas Raiders Favorite: Seahawks –6.5 Game Total: 40.5 Implied Point Total: Seahawks 23.5, Raiders 17 Seahawks Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba Seahawks RBs In Week 8, both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to action against the Chicago Bears in a gross, ugly backfield split that didn’t benefit either back. In Week 9 against a softer opponent in the Cardinals, the Seahawks were able to get the running game going a little bit in neutral and positive game scripts. Both players were heavily involved, but Charbonnet saw more work than Price. Charbonnet (17) out-touched Price (13), and George Holani was essentially phased out of regular work with just two snaps. Charbonnet was the lead back on the game’s first two drives, after which Price and Charbonnet alternated drives for the rest of the game. Price actually led the Seahawks with 54 receiving yards in a very muted game started by Drew Lock . In this configuration, Charbonnet is ahead of Price for now, and in most situations, Charbonnet should get the edge in receiving work. Think of it as the early Kyren Williams/Blake Corum split, but with Corum getting a bit more of the receiving work while Williams plays the majority of the snaps. Charbonnet certainly isn’t Williams, but if Seattle can find some offensive rhythm, both backs can achieve fantasy viability. Fantasy Advice: With the Raiders giving up the second-most fantasy points per game to backfields, this is a great spot for the Seahawks backs. I’d be happy to fire up Charbonnet as a low-end RB2 and Price as a low-end flex play who should get enough work to matter here. item.content:encoded: Hey, folks! We’re back with our third and final block of games for the Week 10 NFL slate, and we’re covering all three late games, Sunday Night Football and Monday Night Football! We’ve compiled the game groupings here to make it easier to find the games you want: Block 1: WAS-NYG, NE-DET, KC-ATL, HOU-CLE, MIA-IND Block 2: JAC-TEN, MIN-GB, CAR-NO, BUF-NYJ Block 3: SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN, LAC-BAL “The Outlook” will give you the details, stats, analysis, recommendations and everything else you need to make informed fantasy football decisions. Every fantasy-relevant player on each team will be profiled in this article. We want everyone reading this to bring home championships in their fantasy leagues! I’m incredibly excited to bring this article to all of you this season, and I hope you enjoy the ride. If you have any questions, feel free to find me on Bluesky (@ktompkinsii.bsky.social) or tag me in a post with any lineup questions. I’ll do my best to answer them for you. Let’s get into it! All game and implied point totals listed were compiled via DraftKings Sportsbook on Thursday for SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN and LAC-BAL. Teams on bye in Week 9: Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas Raiders Favorite: Seahawks –6.5 Game Total: 40.5 Implied Point Total: Seahawks 23.5, Raiders 17 Seahawks Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba Seahawks RBs In Week 8, both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to action against the Chicago Bears in a gross, ugly backfield split that didn’t benefit either back. In Week 9 against a softer opponent in the Cardinals, the Seahawks were able to get the running game going a little bit in neutral and positive game scripts. Both players were heavily involved, but Charbonnet saw more work than Price. Charbonnet (17) out-touched Price (13), and George Holani was essentially phased out of regular work with just two snaps. Charbonnet was the lead back on the game’s first two drives, after which Price and Charbonnet alternated drives for the rest of the game. Price actually led the Seahawks with 54 receiving yards in a very muted game started by Drew Lock . In this configuration, Charbonnet is ahead of Price for now, and in most situations, Charbonnet should get the edge in receiving work. Think of it as the early Kyren Williams/Blake Corum split, but with Corum getting a bit more of the receiving work while Williams plays the majority of the snaps. Charbonnet certainly isn’t Williams, but if Seattle can find some offensive rhythm, both backs can achieve fantasy viability. Fantasy Advice: With the Raiders giving up the second-most fantasy points per game to backfields, this is a great spot for the Seahawks backs. I’d be happy to fire up Charbonnet as a low-end RB2 and Price as a low-end flex play who should get enough work to matter here. Raiders Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: TE Brock Bowers QB Fernando Mendoza With Kirk Cousins now back in Pizza Ranch country , Mendoza will make his first NFL start after watching Cousins for nine games and getting some garbage-time throws in Week 5’s blowout loss in New England. Mendoza will immediately be thrown into the fire at home against the Seahawks before having to travel to Denver to play the Broncos. More than likely, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko and head coach and playcaller Klint Kubiak will do their best not to put too much on Mendoza’s plate early on. That means conservative playcalling and getting the ball out quickly. It may also mean more running plays, so we’ll see how the Raiders navigate these waters over the next few weeks. Fantasy Advice: Mendoza is worth picking up as a speculative stash. Trusting him as a fantasy starter against Seattle? I doubt anybody is that desperate, unless you are exactly that: desperate. Raiders RBs The split among these Vegas running backs persists, and Mike Washington Jr. took a bit of a backseat to Ashton Jeanty in terms of touches and overall playing time. Jeanty handled an overwhelming 63% of the snaps and 73% of the routes, earning seven targets and catching five passes for -5 yards. I’m sure the anti-PPR bros were up in arms about Jeanty earning seven points on that receiving work and his 25 rushing yards. Meanwhile, Washington’s -0.5 yards per carry likely isn’t impressing anybody. Jeanty has a bit of R.J. Harvey in him right now with his role, and Washington is somebody you don’t need to be plugging into your fantasy lineups. Luckily, Jeanty’s receiving floor could pay some dividends for a young quarterback making his first NFL start. Fantasy Advice: I’d be fine with Jeanty as a flex against the Seahawks in Week 10, but his fantasy stock has really fallen over the last month with Kubiak’s meddling. To be fair, Jeanty hasn’t exactly helped himself here, despite reportedly being banged up. Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals Favorite: Rams –9.5 Game Total: 39.5 Implied Point Total: Rams 24.5, Cardinals 15 Rams Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: None QB Matthew Stafford It’s been the running game that has carried Stafford’s offense over the past month. Stafford’s best fantasy finish was QB11 against the Raiders in Week 7. Since then, he’s finished as QB22 against the Chargers and QB20 against the Commanders. He hasn’t had Davante Adams in any of those three games. Now, at least for the foreseeable future, he won’t have Puka Nacua either. You could still make the case for starting Stafford with Nacua in the lineup. Without him, however, it’s a collection of young, inexperienced players, his running backs and a glut of tight ends. That doesn’t make for a very enticing fantasy quarterback, especially when the Rams’ running backs have been driving the offense and they have a below-average matchup against fantasy running backs on tap. I’d be looking elsewhere, despite the Cardinals being one of the best matchups for any quarterback. Fantasy Advice: Stafford is a solid QB2 option who should be able to provide a usable floor, but a ceiling game is almost impossible to expect given the injuries to both Adams and Nacua. Rams RBs This Rams offense will have to rely almost entirely on Kyren Williams and Blake Corum for now, with Adams and Nacua out of the wide receiver lineup. Luckily, Corum has been on a massive heater with five consecutive top-20 fantasy finishes and at least 58 yards and a touchdown in each of those games. Meanwhile, Williams should be able to pick up some of the target-earning slack without Nacua while continuing to provide solid production on the ground. Williams had his worst fantasy performance of the season, finishing as RB25 last week with three receptions and 61 yards from scrimmage against the Commanders. However, if there’s a time for anybody to pick up the pieces of the offense after these two major injuries, it’s now for both Williams and Corum. Fantasy Advice: Both Williams and Corum are viable fantasy RB2s against the Cardinals, with Williams getting a slight edge in PPR formats and the two being nearly even in value in half-PPR. Cardinals Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: TE Trey McBride RB Tyler Allgeier It feels like Allgeier’s 36.1 fantasy-point outburst against the Cowboys was quite the outlier, as he went right back to averaging 2.7 yards per carry against the Seahawks. To be fair, that was expected. The outburst came against the Cowboys, and he returned to being a plodder against the Seahawks in Seattle. Even more factors are working against him now. Allgeier faces another tough defense at home in Week 10 against the Rams, and Bam Knight may return to work in tandem with him. With Gardner Minshew injured and placed on IR, rookie Carson Beck will start at quarterback this weekend. That combination of factors really pushes Allgeier down the rankings and makes him a volume-based back who may not even get enough opportunities if Knight returns and takes some carries away fro

item.title: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'
item.description: Pat Cummins spent over an hour fielding questions over sandpapergate on Friday [Getty Images] As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers. Outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that. But inside the nets at Cricket Central in Sydney, he faced more than a dozen TV cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest. "I don't want to talk about this again after today," he said. "Even if it takes all day... I'll stay here until we have no more questions." A book by his friend and former teammate Usman Khawaja has renewed scrutiny on a 2018 plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's third Test match against South Africa in Cape Town. Three players admitted they were involved at the time and were handed lengthy bans, but in a memoir released last week, Khawaja said the entire Australian team knew about the sandpaper scheme. His claims have plunged the Australian cricket world into chaos, thrown speculation over key figures from that Test - including star bowler Cummins who has since risen to hold what many joke is Australia's most important job - and reopened wounds for fans. Josh, 28, told the BBC he thought everyone had moved on: "It's just a bit crazy that it's all blown up again... I think it is a bit ridiculous, after eight years." "I'm a bit bored of it," another spectator at the New South Wales vs South Australia Sheffield Shield match said. Josh says he was surprised the scandal is back in the news [BBC] Among fans, there's frustration that Khawaja has chosen to come forward now, almost a decade on and at the start of an exciting summer, and year, of cricket. Though there's an argument there'd never be a good time for Khawaja, who retired from international cricket in January, to make these allegations. There's worry about the impact on the men's team's performance this summer, after a lacklustre showing in South Africa last month - its first Test matches there since the 2018 incident. There's a sense of injustice that Australia can't escape the scandal, given - according to many players themselves - how common boundary-bending on ball tampering apparently was in that era. "It's a bit of a stitch up," 21-year-old James said. "Every country has done it... if it wasn't us, it was probably going to be someone else." Khawaja has said he owed it to the three players punished to tell his side of the story [Getty Images] Khawaja's memoir is also causing rancour among current and former players and coaches. item.content:encoded: Pat Cummins spent over an hour fielding questions over sandpapergate on Friday [Getty Images] As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers. Outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that. But inside the nets at Cricket Central in Sydney, he faced more than a dozen TV cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest. "I don't want to talk about this again after today," he said. "Even if it takes all day... I'll stay here until we have no more questions." A book by his friend and former teammate Usman Khawaja has renewed scrutiny on a 2018 plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's third Test match against South Africa in Cape Town. Three players admitted they were involved at the time and were handed lengthy bans, but in a memoir released last week, Khawaja said the entire Australian team knew about the sandpaper scheme. His claims have plunged the Australian cricket world into chaos, thrown speculation over key figures from that Test - including star bowler Cummins who has since risen to hold what many joke is Australia's most important job - and reopened wounds for fans. Josh, 28, told the BBC he thought everyone had moved on: "It's just a bit crazy that it's all blown up again... I think it is a bit ridiculous, after eight years." "I'm a bit bored of it," another spectator at the New South Wales vs South Australia Sheffield Shield match said. Josh says he was surprised the scandal is back in the news [BBC] Among fans, there's frustration that Khawaja has chosen to come forward now, almost a decade on and at the start of an exciting summer, and year, of cricket. Though there's an argument there'd never be a good time for Khawaja, who retired from international cricket in January, to make these allegations. There's worry about the impact on the men's team's performance this summer, after a lacklustre showing in South Africa last month - its first Test matches there since the 2018 incident. There's a sense of injustice that Australia can't escape the scandal, given - according to many players themselves - how common boundary-bending on ball tampering apparently was in that era. "It's a bit of a stitch up," 21-year-old James said. "Every country has done it... if it wasn't us, it was probably going to be someone else." Khawaja has said he owed it to the three players punished to tell his side of the story [Getty Images] Khawaja's memoir is also causing rancour among current and former players and coaches. In it, he said he had wanted the team to take collective responsibility for the tampering after batsman Cameron Bancroft was caught with the sandpaper on field. "I said: 'Take this as a team. We did this as a team. We knew what was going on, and we have to take it as a team'." However Khawaja has since said he didn't want to start a "witch hunt" and has refused to answer questions on exactly who he claims knew of the scheme, and what they knew. David Warner, who received the most severe punishment of the Cape Town trio, said Khawaja had written the truth and that Cummins' press conference denying the claims "threw him under the bus". Steve Smith, the captain at the time who was also suspended, has been travelling overseas and is yet to say anything publicly about the claims in the book. Bancroft is also staying silent for now despite previously suggesting the bowlers knew. But half of Australia's living cricket royalty and a slew of former coaches - some of whom have been accused of wrongdoing too - have thrown in their two cents. And Cricket Australia is under pressure from some to reopen its investigation into sandpapergate - something chief executive Todd Greenberg has already ruled out. Prof David Rowe of the University of Western Sydney told the BBC the saga was still so painful for many players and fans as the country sees itself as "a nation of good sports". "The idea of being a good sport is two things. One is being good at sport, so you actually win. But the other side is that you do it honourably and fairly," he said. "Many Australians would see themselves as above all that. That is: cheating is what other teams get up to... not the nation of good sports." He said the revelation was a "nasty shock" which brought the country "collective shame" which lingers today. He says he doubts that the cricket scene would be able to move on without a fresh response from the governing body, Cricket Australia. "One of the best ways to fuel conspiracy theories and keep sandpapergate going is to essentially say 'there's no more to see here' - especially when that comes from the authorities," Rowe said. Australia kicked off it's summer with an ODI against England on Friday [Getty Images] Asked about a fresh investigation, Cummins said it was a matter for Cricket Australia. Over the marathon press conference - which one reporter suggested was the longest in Australian sporting history - Cummins was cautious, pausing often to consider his responses and to make sure they answered the questions being asked of him. But he was also frank - using strong words to reject what he said were "vague" claims by Khawaja and admitting he was frustrated a friend had put him in this position. "Friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations... That's something I've been grappling with the last couple of days." As the reporters ran out of steam, Cummins said it was "annoying" that sandpapergate scandal was still a distraction for Australian cricket. He gestured outside to the Sheffield Shield match and mentioning Friday's one-day international against England in Perth, from which he and other key players are being rested. "It's been eight years... Hopefully today we put a line through it and we're done and we can all move on to much more fun topics, like actual cricket." Few people think he'll get his wish. "It's going to be hard to move on, given that there's two sides of the story and it doesn't look like either side is going to back down," James said. "I don't know what the outcome will be." item.title: 5 smartphones with the best zoom cameras in 2026
item.description: Smartphone cameras have become increasingly sophisticated in 2026, with manufacturers competing to deliver sharper photographs, improved low-light performance and, particularly, better zoom capabilities. One of the biggest developments has been the introduction of more advanced periscope telephoto cameras, larger image sensors and optical zoom systems capable of capturing distant subjects without relying entirely on digital enlargement. These improvements have made it possible to photograph wildlife, sporting events, concerts, buildings and other distant subjects with a level of detail that was previously difficult to achieve with a smartphone. While several manufacturers advertise zoom capabilities of up to 100x or 120x, the actual quality of photographs at those magnifications varies considerably. Optical zoom, sensor size, optical image stabilisation and image processing are therefore more important considerations than the maximum zoom figure alone. Here are five smartphones with some of the best zoom camera systems available in 2026, based on their camera hardware and independent reviews. 1. Oppo Find X9 Ultra The Oppo Find X9 Ultra stands out as one of the most capable zoom smartphones of 2026, particularly because it features two dedicated telephoto cameras rather than relying on a single zoom lens. The smartphone comes with a 200-megapixel primary telephoto camera offering 3x optical zoom and a separate 50-megapixel periscope telephoto camera capable of 10x optical zoom. The combination gives users greater flexibility when photographing subjects at different distances, from portraits and street photography to distant buildings, wildlife and performers at concerts. Its 10x optical zoom is particularly important because it allows the camera to magnify distant subjects using its dedicated optical hardware rather than simply enlarging pixels digitally. According to Digital Trends, the phone can extend its zoom capabilities to 120x digitally. Its 200-megapixel telephoto camera also provides additional room for cropping images while retaining useful detail. The publication highlights the phone’s impressive telephoto sharpness, autofocus performance and ability to capture distant subjects. For people who regularly photograph sporting events, wildlife or concerts, the Find X9 Ultra is a particularly compelling option. 2. Huawei Pura 80 Ultra The Huawei Pura 80 Ultra is another smartphone that deserves recognition for its unusual approach to long-range photography. Its biggest attraction is a switchable dual-telephoto camera system that offers 3.7x and 9.4x optical zoom. Unlike conventional smartphones that use separate telephoto sensors for different magnification levels, Huawei developed a system in which two telephoto lenses share a large 50-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch sensor. A moving optical mechanism switches between the two lenses, allowing users to photograph subjects at different distances while maintaining the benefits of optical magnification

item.content:encoded: Smartphone cameras have become increasingly sophisticated in 2026, with manufacturers competing to deliver sharper photographs, improved low-light performance and, particularly, better zoom capabilities. One of the biggest developments has been the introduction of more advanced periscope telephoto cameras, larger image sensors and optical zoom systems capable of capturing distant subjects without relying entirely on digital enlargement. These improvements have made it possible to photograph wildlife, sporting events, concerts, buildings and other distant subjects with a level of detail that was previously difficult to achieve with a smartphone. While several manufacturers advertise zoom capabilities of up to 100x or 120x, the actual quality of photographs at those magnifications varies considerably. Optical zoom, sensor size, optical image stabilisation and image processing are therefore more important considerations than the maximum zoom figure alone. Here are five smartphones with some of the best zoom camera systems available in 2026, based on their camera hardware and independent reviews. 1. Oppo Find X9 Ultra The Oppo Find X9 Ultra stands out as one of the most capable zoom smartphones of 2026, particularly because it features two dedicated telephoto cameras rather than relying on a single zoom lens. The smartphone comes with a 200-megapixel primary telephoto camera offering 3x optical zoom and a separate 50-megapixel periscope telephoto camera capable of 10x optical zoom. The combination gives users greater flexibility when photographing subjects at different distances, from portraits and street photography to distant buildings, wildlife and performers at concerts. Its 10x optical zoom is particularly important because it allows the camera to magnify distant subjects using its dedicated optical hardware rather than simply enlarging pixels digitally. According to Digital Trends, the phone can extend its zoom capabilities to 120x digitally. Its 200-megapixel telephoto camera also provides additional room for cropping images while retaining useful detail. The publication highlights the phone’s impressive telephoto sharpness, autofocus performance and ability to capture distant subjects. For people who regularly photograph sporting events, wildlife or concerts, the Find X9 Ultra is a particularly compelling option. 2. Huawei Pura 80 Ultra The Huawei Pura 80 Ultra is another smartphone that deserves recognition for its unusual approach to long-range photography. Its biggest attraction is a switchable dual-telephoto camera system that offers 3.7x and 9.4x optical zoom. Unlike conventional smartphones that use separate telephoto sensors for different magnification levels, Huawei developed a system in which two telephoto lenses share a large 50-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch sensor. A moving optical mechanism switches between the two lenses, allowing users to photograph subjects at different distances while maintaining the benefits of optical magnification. The 9.4x telephoto camera has a 212mm equivalent focal length, making it particularly useful for photographing distant subjects. Huawei also includes optical image stabilisation on both telephoto configurations, helping to reduce camera shake when taking photographs at high magnification. According to DXOMARK’s camera assessment, the Pura 80 Ultra achieved outstanding telephoto performance, with impressive detail preservation, low noise and accurate colour reproduction. Its digital zoom extends to 100x. However, the phone comes with an important consideration for international buyers: Huawei devices do not offer native Google Mobile Services support, which may affect access to familiar Android applications. 3. Vivo X300 Ultra Vivo has continued to push the boundaries of smartphone photography with the X300 Ultra, particularly through its advanced telephoto camera and optional external zoom accessories. The smartphone features a 200-megapixel periscope telephoto camera with a 3.7x optical zoom capability, supported by optical image stabilisation. Its large telephoto sensor helps preserve details when photographing distant subjects, making it suitable for wildlife photography, portraits and outdoor events. However, one of its most interesting features is its compatibility with an optional telephoto extender. According to Android Authority, Vivo offers a second-generation external telephoto lens that extends the camera’s reach to approximately 400mm equivalent, or around 17x magnification. This accessory allows users to photograph subjects much farther away than they ordinarily could with a conventional smartphone camera. DXOMARK also praised the X300 Ultra’s telephoto performance, highlighting its ability to preserve details across different zoom ranges, including at longer distances. There are limitations, however. The external lens adds bulk, and image quality can deteriorate in challenging lighting conditions, particularly when AI processing becomes more aggressive. Nevertheless, for photography enthusiasts who want to experiment with extreme-distance smartphone photography, the X300 Ultra is among the most interesting options in 2026. 4. Xiaomi 17 Ultra The Xiaomi 17 Ultra takes a different approach to smartphone zoom photography by introducing a mechanically variable telephoto lens. Rather than depending entirely on fixed optical zoom levels, the smartphone uses a 200-megapixel telephoto camera with a variable focal length covering approximately 75mm to 100mm, equivalent to 3.2x to 4.3x optical zoom. This allows users to adjust their framing within that range without relying on digital cropping between fixed magnification levels. The telephoto camera also features optical image stabilisation and a large 1/1.4-inch sensor, helping it capture detailed photographs in different lighting conditions. Its Leica camera partnership further contributes to its photography capabilities, with colour profiles and processing options designed to give users greater creative control. According to Digital Trends, the Xiaomi 17 Ultra can extend its zoom capabilities to 120x digitally, while its large telephoto sensor provides additional flexibility for cropping images. The device also supports advanced video recording features, including 8K recording and 4K at up to 120 frames per second. Although its native optical zoom range is shorter than that of the Oppo Find X9 Ultra and Huawei Pura 80 Ultra, its mechanically adjustable telephoto lens makes it an interesting choice for photographers who value flexibility and image quality. 5. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra Samsung remains a major competitor in smartphone zoom photography with the Galaxy S26 Ultra. The device features a 200-megapixel primary camera alongside two dedicated telephoto cameras: a 10-megapixel camera with 3x optical zoom and a 50-megapixel periscope camera with 5x optical zoom. The two telephoto cameras give users different magnification options for photographing subjects at varying distances. Its 5x optical zoom is particularly useful for portraits, travel photography and capturing distant objects, while the 3x camera provides a shorter telephoto option for everyday photography. Samsung also offers up to 10x optical-quality zoom and 100x Space Zoom, combining optical hardware with computational photography to extend its reach. The Galaxy S26 Ultra benefits from optical image stabilisation and Samsung’s image-processing technology, which help improve sharpness and reduce camera shake when photographing distant subjects. One of its biggest advantages over some of the other smartphones on this list is its established global retail and software ecosystem. However, its 5x optical zoom means it does not offer the same native long-range reach as the Oppo Find X9 Ultra or Huawei Pura 80 Ultra. item.title: Palantir's NHS cancer app gets plenty of praise, precious few users
item.description: Only a handful of NHS trusts are using the cancer app on the controversial £330 million Federated Data Platform (FDP) run by Palantir, while newly released figures raise questions about which trusts are benefiting. Cancer 360 was designed to bring cancer patients' data from disparate spreadsheets and electronic health records into a central system, helping health professionals prioritize treatment. Pilots began four years ago, and trusts are not charged directly for the FDP. Yet official figures put Cancer 360's uptake at just five or six trusts. Freedom of Information responses gathered by grassroots campaign group No Palantir in the NHS also reveal discrepancies between reported benefits and recorded use. In June 2025, NHS England said that Cancer 360 "drastically cut down diagnosis times" and referred to a pilot at Chelsea and Westminster NHS Foundation Trust, which saw the proportion of patients diagnosed within 28 days climb from 72 percent to 85 percent. The trust began trials in 2022, while working with Palantir under a £23 million contract awarded without competition, before the US firm was awarded the FDP contract in late 2023. Critics argued the FDP procurement was flawed as Palantir had developed use cases under £60 million in non-competitive contracts which were then carried over to the FDP. Last year, NHS England said Cancer 360 served 46 registered teams and 239 active users, and processed 52,000 patients. In June 2026, NHS England said there were five trusts using Cancer 360 as of March 2026. Of those, only two were listed as benefiting. In July, health minister Preet Kaur Gill repeated the five-trust usage figure in a Parliamentary answer . Official data released in October said that as of June, six trusts were using Cancer 360 and five were benefiting, but did not identify the trusts or explain the increase. The stats have since been removed from the NHS England website but are archived here . In June, NHS England responded to a Freedom of Information request . It said six trusts reported unique users logging into the Cancer 360 app over the last 12 months. However, two trusts cited as having run successful pilots – Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and Royal United Hospitals Bath – were listed as having zero unique users logging into the system during that period, according to NHS England's reply. Both trusts were said to have received benefits from the system, according to a FoI response sent to campaign group Foxglove in June this year. The Register asked both trusts and NHS England to explain the discrepancy. One of the six trusts said to be logging into the cancer app, East Lancashire Hospitals, reported just one unique user. It later confirmed in an FoI response in August that it was not live with the FDP. It had planned to adopt the platform, leading with Cancer 360, but did not have a date for going live with the app. No Palantir in the NHS also identified trusts that considered Cancer 360 but decided against adopting it.

In July, health minister Preet Kaur Gill repeated the five-trust usage figure in a Parliamentary answer . Official data released in October said that as of June, six trusts were using Cancer 360 and five were benefiting, but did not identify the trusts or explain the increase. The stats have since been removed from the NHS England website but are archived here . In June, NHS England responded to a Freedom of Information request . It said six trusts reported unique users logging into the Cancer 360 app over the last 12 months. However, two trusts cited as having run successful pilots – Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and Royal United Hospitals Bath – were listed as having zero unique users logging into the system during that period, according to NHS England's reply. Both trusts were said to have received benefits from the system, according to a FoI response sent to campaign group Foxglove in June this year. The Register asked both trusts and NHS England to explain the discrepancy. One of the six trusts said to be logging into the cancer app, East Lancashire Hospitals, reported just one unique user. It later confirmed in an FoI response in August that it was not live with the FDP. It had planned to adopt the platform, leading with Cancer 360, but did not have a date for going live with the app. No Palantir in the NHS also identified trusts that considered Cancer 360 but decided against adopting it. East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust considered using the app but rejected it because there was "no immediate requirement for it," according to its FoI response . In its FoI response , Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust said it did not adopt the app because of issues around the metadata requirements. Meanwhile, official figures on cancer diagnosis waiting times show wider improvements across England. Given Cancer 360's limited uptake, those national gains cannot simply be credited to the app. In July this year, the UK's statistical regulator told NHS England to ensure ministers are briefed accurately following a row over data used to promote the purported benefits of the Palantir-run FDP. Campaign group Foxglove had found that nearly a third of NHS trusts using Palantir's health data platform were performing fewer patient procedures than before it went live and that Chelsea and Westminster Hospital accounted for 84 percent of the reported fall in outpatient waiting lists, while only 16 trusts were using the FDP tool. The Office for Statistics Regulation began assessing NHS England's claims about the FDP's performance and the quango included more caveats on its website. Scrutiny of the FDP's reported benefits comes as the government decides whether to continue the Palantir-led contract beyond February 2027. The initial contract was provided for a term of up to seven years, with a maximum value of £330 million. Reports this week suggest the government is set to renew the contract , but run a parallel procurement to find an alternative to Palantir as pressure mounts to reduce lock-in to a single vendor and boost sovereign technology. Palantir was founded with startup money from a CIA-linked VC firm and has relied on close ties with the US intelligence, military, and immigration services since its inception, although its recent growth in the wider business market is notable. ®

item.title: Microsoft outage live: UK police, NHS services and schools affected amid ongoing global disruption
item.description: Microsoft reports it is seeing some ‘positive results’ in its efforts to get its services back online for millions of customers around the world. Tell us: have you been affected by the Microsoft outage? Microsoft struggles to fix huge outage affecting Outlook and Teams What happened and when will it be fixed? There are plenty of essential services that remain unaffected by the outage, which is largely impacting email systems. The Australian Medical Association said it has so far not received any reports that hospitals or clinics are impacted. Impact is largely restricted to the sending and receiving of email. Western Australia, along with jurisdictions around the world, is being impacted by a global Microsoft outage. We are receiving updates from the Commonwealth who are working with Microsoft at the most senior levels to resolve. Microsoft are prioritising life, safety and Government services. Continue reading...

item.title: Joe Root scripts history against Australia, becomes only third England player to enter elite 200 list
item.description: England batting mainstay Joe Root on Friday became only the third player from the country to feature in 200 One-Day Internationals (ODIs). Root reached the milestone when he took the field for the first ODI against Australia at Perth Stadium. He joined Eoin Morgan, who played 225 ODIs, and Jos Buttler, who has 204 appearances, in the list of England players to reach the landmark. Australia captain Mitch Marsh won the toss and elected to bowl in the series opener, which comes amid renewed attention on the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal. Less than four hours before the toss, Australia Test captain Pat Cummins addressed a news conference in Sydney, dismissing claims made in Usman Khawaja’s autobiography, released this week, as “complete and utter nonsense.” Marsh said the opening ODI of the three-match series would be an important start to a busy 12 months for Australia, which includes a home Test series against New Zealand, tours of India and England, and next year's World Cup in South Africa. “It’s the start of the summer for us (and) that first game is always important,” he said. Australia will be without several of their first-choice fast bowlers for the white-ball series, with Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Scott Boland missing from the squad. Xavier Bartlett, left-arm pacer Spencer Johnson and 21-year-old Mahli Beardman are part of the bowling attack instead. Beardman, who hails from Western Australia, is making his international debut. Marsh said the young fast bowler would have a special occasion playing his first international match at home. “It’s going to be exciting for him. No better place in the world for a young West Australian to debut,” Marsh said. “We've got a reasonably young and inexperienced side, but lots of energy.” Australia are playing their first ODI since September, when they lost a three-match series 2-1 against South Africa. 135794817

item.title: Disgruntled US tenant kills building manager, injures four, shoots self
item.description: A disgruntled tenant shot dead his building manager and wounded four other people in an upscale neighborhood of Washington on Thursday before killing himself, police said amid a massive law enforcement response that shut down part of the city. The shooting, which occurred about a mile north of the White House, sparked a massive police response in the nation’s capital with dozens of law enforcement vehicles racing to the scene and police helicopters hovering overhead. Dramatic dispatch audio captured the initial callout for a shooting inside the gym just before 8 am (0100 GMT). Within minutes a breathless police officer could be heard telling the dispatcher “we have an active shooter” and requesting the SWAT team. Jeffery Carroll, Washington’s interim police chief, told reporters that the gunman, identified as Matt Lambert, 55, had been involved in an ongoing dispute over maintenance with the condominium association for the building where he owned an apartment. Lambert, an emergency medicine physician, fatally shot the building manager, James Stuart, 46, in a packed gym attached to the complex, located in the Logan Circle neighborhood. Lambert then barricaded himself in his seventh-floor unit, Carroll said. He then opened fire from his balcony on people below, wounding four. One of the wounded was in critical condition while the others did not have life-threatening injuries. The Washington Post reported that construction workers from a nearby jobsite were among the injured, citing a company executive. Lambert fired at least twice at police through his apartment door and set the unit on fire before shooting himself, Carroll said. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Photos and video quickly emerged on social media of police in tactical gear surrounding the building with rifles drawn as well as fire emerging from an exterior wall. Carroll said Lambert had taken legal action against the homeowners association of the condominium complex where he lived over what he considered to be a lack of maintenance of the building. An X feed reportedly linked to Lambert titled @OfMiceandMold is a litany of complaints about mold and water damage. The final post, described as a “manifesto,” is an engineering report detailing problems with his apartment. Washington Mayor Muriel Bowser denounced what she described as a “senseless act of gun violence.” The shooting occurred during the busy morning rush hour, snarling traffic as police closed off streets around the area and evacuated residents. The Washington Sun quoted a member of the VIDA Fitness gym as saying that he was on a treadmill at the workout facility when the shooting began. Michael Carney said he heard a “pop” and then saw someone on the gym floor who had been shot in the head. “Everyone was kind of just hiding behind planters and stuff,” Carney told The Sun. item.title: Pochettino to take over at Manchester United; Grealish apologises to Everton fans: football – live
item.description: USMNT head coach is due to speak later on Friday Today’s fixtures | Follow us on TikTok | Mail David Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be appointed as the new Manchester United head coach later today. The Argentinian will leave his role with the United States to sign a two-and-a-half year contract at Old Trafford as Michael Carrick’s replacement. Carrick and his backroom staff were dismissed on Thursday, with Pochettino expected to bring his trusted lieutenants from previous roles with him. Friday 13 November: United are set to confirm his appointment. Saturday 14 November: He takes charge of the USA in the first leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti in Miami (9.30pm UK time). Tuesday 17 November: He leads the USA for the last time, in the second leg against Haiti in Cincinnati (midnight UK time). Wednesday 18 November: He flies to Manchester to meet his new bosses. Thursday 19 November: He takes his first training session with the players. Sunday 22 November: His first game in charge is Liverpool away at Anfield (4.30pm). Gulp! Continue reading...

item.title: Tom Brady Ranks Chicago Bears Above Bills Despite Worse Record
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Tom Brady has placed the 7-2 Chicago Bears at the top of his latest NFL power rankings, even though the Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers hold better records. The NFL legend explained his logic via Fox Sports after the Bears beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He noted that his list requires a team to lose a game to drop from the first spot. “Yeah and in my rankings, you got to lose to fall out of the top spot,” Brady said. The quarterback admitted that Caleb Williams made things difficult with four interceptions during the recent win, yet Chicago remains number one for now. Brady believes great teams must win ugly sometimes, pointing to how the defense created pressure all night long. He also highlighted Cairo Santos for coming up clutch to win the game in the final seconds. The Bye Week Question Brady paused to consider a specific scenario regarding the current schedule. The Bears have not lost since Williams returned from his injury, and now they get a bye week to clean things up. Brady wondered what happens to the number one team when they sit out a week. If the Bears remain inactive, Buffalo could surge to the summit, according to his suggestion that the door might be open. The Bills beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9 to earn their spot in second place. Per Yahoo Sports , the Jaguars took fifth place after going 6-2 following their win over the Baltimore Ravens. Within this specific ranking list, they stand as the sole team boasting six wins to reach the top five. The Denver Broncos hold fourth place at 7-2, while the 49ers come in at third after beating the Las Vegas Raiders. A report from Windy City Gridiron lists the San Francisco 49ers as the number one team, arguing they have been the league’s best since week one. That same source places the Chicago Bears at number two, noting they are the best team if every squad plays its best game. The report emphasizes that Chicago proved it can win even when it does not have its A game, as shown against Tampa. Player Performance and Midseason Awards The Bears are currently in their bye week after securing a 7-2 start to the year. According to Bear Goggles On , the team finds itself in first place in the NFC North despite some ups and downs. The source highlights defensive end Austin Booker as a key winner for the team this season. It also names Kyler Gordon as the Comeback Player of the Year after he racked up 13 tackles and four sacks in four games. Rookie Dillon Thieneman leads the Bears in tackles with 57, plus five pass deflections and two tackles for loss. The versatile weapon has shown a mix of linebacker and defensive back skills while Coby Bryant sits out. Despite an encouraging Week 9 showing versus the Buccaneers, Jaylon Johnson has allowed a 104.9 passer rating this year. item.title: Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown trending toward return vs. 49ers after injury update
item.description: Chris Jones-Imagn Images Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown trending toward return vs. 49ers after injury update appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . DeMarvion Overshown is looking for redemption after drawing a puzzling unsportsmanlike penalty during the Dallas Cowboys ’ Week 9 win versus the Indianapolis Colts, and it appears he will get the chance to earn it this Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers. The 2023 third-round draft pick is trending toward playing after posting full practice participation on Thursday, via Clarence Hill Jr. The Cowboys have a lengthy injury report, but it might get a little lighter come Friday. Overshown has dealt with hamstring and back injuries throughout the 2026 campaign and was inactive for the Colts game. That did not stop him from celebrating a big fumble recovery with his teammates on the field , a rule violation that cost Dallas 15 yards. The 26-year-old linebacker accepted responsibility for the mistake, but he probably still feels inclined to make a grand gesture on the gridiron. Forcing a turnover of his own or getting a big stop would probably suffice. Overshown has one interception, one forced fumble, 20 combined tackles and two passes defended in three games played. He is in the final year of his contract and is therefore running out of time to drive up his market value and wow executives. An impactful performance versus the 49ers, one of the current favorites to win Super Bowl 61, would surely help his cause. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) And it would breathe new life into the unsteady Cowboys. Dallas (4-5) can apply pressure to the New York Giants and pull within one game of first place in the NFC East. When in uniform, DeMarvion Overshown can be a positive presence for a run defense that is surrendering an NFC-worst 147.4 yards per week. Barring an unforeseen setback, he will line up opposite the 49ers (7-1) inside AT&T Stadium. The action will kick off at 4:25 p.m. ET. Related: 49ers’ George Kittle might wear his NSFW anti-Cowboys shirt in Week 10 clash Related: What Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown said about boneheaded penalty during Colts game

item.title: Will Ferguson-inspired Pochettino succeed where Carrick failed at Man Utd?
item.description: Maurucio Pochettino (right) was first mentioned as a contender to manage Manchester United when Louis van Gaal was sacked in May 2016 [Getty Images] When Mauricio Pochettino was asked the three Premier League managers he would have loved to have played for, he was unequivocal. "Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson," replied Pochettino, who is set to be the next manager of Manchester United. In 2023, the Argentine - then at Chelsea, and dressed in full Blues training gear - was being interviewed by Sky Sports. Still he felt a need to express his adoration for Ferguson. Six years prior to that interview, while managing Tottenham, he had shared lunch with the legendary former United manager. "When I was young, when I started my career as a manager, he was always my inspiration, my reference," Pochettino said. "And when you can share two hours with a person who was the greatest manager in the history of football, you can only enjoy." Hiring United managers has been complicated since Ferguson's departure in 2013, and one of the most prominent complications has been a back-and-forth around the club's DNA. For some, winning by any means necessary should take precedence, while others believe the style of play and cultural heritage of United's most successful period is vital to the club's identity. In recent years, United's managerial merry-go-round has alternated between European coaches with their own fixed styles of play, and former players from the Ferguson era. But between his tactics of choice and his adoration for the former United boss, Pochettino may be uniquely placed to bridge the gap between both camps. Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better Michael Carrick's United produced a series of good results to finish last season with a run unmatched by any other team in the league. They looked great, but it was a greatness built on attacking in a transition-heavy manner. Under Carrick, in games they had less than 50% of the ball, they only lost once. In those 13 games, they boasted a win-rate of 62%. This dropped to 36% in games they had the majority of possession. This style of play suited their direct attackers and protected their defenders. At the same time, Casemiro's set-piece prowess provided United a reliable way to break the deadlock against deep defences - something they have struggled with this season. With United a goal up, opponents stepped forward, giving Carrick's men more space. They could play to their strengths again, attacking quickly. It worked. But teams at the top are reluctant to play in this way. item.content:encoded: Maurucio Pochettino (right) was first mentioned as a contender to manage Manchester United when Louis van Gaal was sacked in May 2016 [Getty Images] When Mauricio Pochettino was asked the three Premier League managers he would have loved to have played for, he was unequivocal. "Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson," replied Pochettino, who is set to be the next manager of Manchester United. In 2023, the Argentine - then at Chelsea, and dressed in full Blues training gear - was being interviewed by Sky Sports. Still he felt a need to express his adoration for Ferguson. Six years prior to that interview, while managing Tottenham, he had shared lunch with the legendary former United manager. "When I was young, when I started my career as a manager, he was always my inspiration, my reference," Pochettino said. "And when you can share two hours with a person who was the greatest manager in the history of football, you can only enjoy." Hiring United managers has been complicated since Ferguson's departure in 2013, and one of the most prominent complications has been a back-and-forth around the club's DNA. For some, winning by any means necessary should take precedence, while others believe the style of play and cultural heritage of United's most successful period is vital to the club's identity. In recent years, United's managerial merry-go-round has alternated between European coaches with their own fixed styles of play, and former players from the Ferguson era. But between his tactics of choice and his adoration for the former United boss, Pochettino may be uniquely placed to bridge the gap between both camps. Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better Michael Carrick's United produced a series of good results to finish last season with a run unmatched by any other team in the league. They looked great, but it was a greatness built on attacking in a transition-heavy manner. Under Carrick, in games they had less than 50% of the ball, they only lost once. In those 13 games, they boasted a win-rate of 62%. This dropped to 36% in games they had the majority of possession. This style of play suited their direct attackers and protected their defenders. At the same time, Casemiro's set-piece prowess provided United a reliable way to break the deadlock against deep defences - something they have struggled with this season. With United a goal up, opponents stepped forward, giving Carrick's men more space. They could play to their strengths again, attacking quickly. It worked. But teams at the top are reluctant to play in this way. Carrick's vision for United was a side that played slick football, with short passes in build-up intuitively, referencing Paris St-Germain's midfield three as a source of inspiration. Building up in this manner, to entice and escape from pressure, before looking to find the forwards quickly, was the plan Carrick was working towards. This didn't come to fruition and trying to take United from a successful counter-attacking side to one that could reliably beat teams while keeping the ball was the same hurdle that undid Ole Gunnar Solskjar and Erik ten Hag. Former players under Sir Alex Ferguson, both Ole Gunnar Solskjar and Michael Carrick leaned into United’s historic style when crafting their game-models [Getty Images] Pochettino gives United an interesting solution to this problem. In his own words, he has described his sides as needing "to be protagonists, always press high, work hard and be dynamic". He refers to himself as a "disciple" of the legendary Argentina boss Marcelo Bielsa, who he played for. If you wanted an immediate comparison in the Premier League to a coach who resembles Pochettino's ideas in possession, it would be worth looking at Liverpool's Andoni Iraola, who similarly cites Bielsa as his reference. These are coaches who, while taking the initiative, encourage vertical football. For as different as the clubs are, both the fans of United and Liverpool have enjoyed success when their teams have played high-octane football. This summer's World Cup was a strong showcase of Pochettino's style of play and his recent tactical adaptation. Rather than a fixed, positional style of play - akin to the work of somebody like Manchester City's Enzo Maresca - Pochettino's USA had only certain players being tasked with holding their position. This approach posed problems for teams who defended in a zonal manner - defending specific areas rather than individual players. The US midfielders being able to move freely meant they could step into areas of the pitch between the zones that were being defended, which resulted in their players often being unmarked with time and space on the ball. By playing in close proximity to each other in the middle of the pitch, the US found another benefit. Small-space passing combinations helped draw the opposing team up towards the ball and combined with clever off-ball movement to stretch the pitch, allowed the US to find their striker with few defenders around him. Pochettino's men looked to thread through-balls in behind and early after enticing the opposition's press and the speedy Folarin Balogun was able to turn those chances into goals. This combination of a fluid midfield, small-space passing and direct through-balls doesn't sound dissimilar to what Carrick was trying to move towards implementing this season. And although that may worry United fans, the similarity in principles will benefit the players. "My philosophy is to give a freer style with a good organisation," were Pochettino's words in 2014. Although philosophically similar, that latter part - a clearer organisation to his freer style - is likely to be what Carrick was unable to reliably offer his players. For fans of top sides, fast-paced, vertical football tends to be accepted when it comes from a place of being proactive - think Ferguson's United or Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool - wanting to keep the ball, but not passing it for passing's sake. Fast-paced, vertical football tends to be frowned upon when it comes from a place of conceding possession and defending your own goal for long periods of the match. The first half of Carrick's stint did appear proactive, while his 4-2-4 press worked well. Leaving four players high was a risk that allowed them to win the ball back and score quickly, but as teams figured this out, United failed to adapt. There also appeared to be a drop in the team's fitness the longer United went from the departure of ex-boss Ruben Amorim, who left United well conditioned, albeit on the back of a schedule without European football. Here we see United's narrow 4-2-4 defensive shape in the first half against Como [Getty Images] Hiring Pochettino will immediately begin the process of turning United into a well-drilled side, capable of applying intense pressure, likely in a co-ordinated manner. Pochettino enjoyed relative success with Spurs, built on this intensity and co-ordination, that differentiated him from the rest of the league. With that unique selling point more common now than a decade ago, how he builds on it will dictate how his tenure unfolds. But watching Brighton this season, he can be assured that an approach founded on intensity off the ball can work in the Premier League in 2026, with Fabian Hurzeler's men second in the league, with the fourth highest average possession, 10 games in. Pochettino, from a footballing point of view, feels extremely aligned to the values of Ferguson's United, and as a result will implement numerous similarities to the things Carrick wanted, but ultimately failed, to deliver. His wealth of experience make him a more proven entity than the departing United manager and if he can get his team fit and pressing high, in typically Pochettino fashion, they should see an upturn in form. item.title: Texans special teams coach is pumped to play in ‘heavenly’ Cleveland weather
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Texans special teams coach is pumped to play in ‘heavenly’ Cleveland weather appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Unlike most players and coaches in the NFL, Houston Texans special teams coordinator Frank Ross relishes playing in inclement weather, as it adds another layer of gamesmanship. The Texans will visit the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, and while some are worried about the windy forecast, Ross is not bothered at all, even though the Browns are still undefeated at home. When a reporter asked him about dealing with the “bad weather” in Cleveland, Ross had a quick counter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I call it good weather! That’s your opinion. I call it good weather! I think we are going to heaven,” said Ross in the video posted by The 33rd Team’s Ari Meirov. He then shared the Texans’ diligence in the challenging situation . “No matter when we go out there, we gotta have to test it. We gonna make sure we make those micro-adjustments relative to which end you’re kicking. Cleveland’s got two different ends. You have to know which way you’re going. To be able to make those and trust your line,” said Ross. #Texans STC Frank Ross on playing in Cleveland this week in “bad weather”: “I call it good weather! That’s your opinion. I call it good weather! I think we are going to heaven.” 😂😂 #FootballGuy pic.twitter.com/AyEMQHV6GS — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 12, 2026 He also expressed excitement for snapper Austin Brinkman, who could play a major role for Houston, as windy weather would deeply affect the offensive strategy of both squads. “Experience. That’s the only way you can improve in that. You gotta go in and do that,” added Ross. “We’ve got two snappers going against each other. They both played at the University of West Virginia. We’re gonna go handle the elements. We know they (Browns) can as well.” The Texans are coming off a win against the Los Angeles Chargers, 44-22, while the Browns are looking to snap a two-game skid. Related: Texans’ Will Anderson Jr. pops up on injury report before Browns game Related: Texans signs former Chiefs WR, return specialist for playoff push

item.title: 'Wrong' and 'nonsense' - Cummins on Khawaja claims
item.description: Pat Cummins was named Australia Test captain in 2021 [Getty Images] Australia captain Pat Cummins has hit back at former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims over the sandpaper scandal, calling them "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense". In 2018, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished for a plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town. Khawaja has published his autobiography this week and the former batter has said the entire Australia team, which included Cummins, knew about the sandpaper scheme and should have taken responsibility. But in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in Sydney, Cummins countered and said: "When he says we all knew, if by that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong. "I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening. "He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense." Cummins and Khawaja played 56 Tests together until Khawaja retired from international cricket in January. Khawaja was in the Australia XI when Cummins made his Test debut in 2011 and the pair were also once team-mates in domestic cricket with New South Wales. "Usman is a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations," said Cummins. "In his book he's been casual with my life and the lives of many others - and, I think, Australian cricket. "I support him to tell his story, 100%, I'm glad he feels like he can, but we have to be accountable for the things that we say and do." In a media conference he arranged himself, Cummins began by promising to answer all questions because, he said: "I don't want to talk about this again after today." At times emotional, Cummins addressed a wide range of topics, including: Advice that some of Khawaja's claims are defamatory, but he will not take legal action He had been in contact with Khawaja and Smith since the book was published, but not Warner His belief that the one-year bans handed to Smith and Warner, and a nine-month suspension to Bancroft were "heavy handed" He had no recollection of Australia tampering with the ball in the 2017-18 Ashes series against England He had met with Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg, who has reviewed the files from the original investigation Explaining why sandpaper would have been present in the dressing room and that it was sometimes used by bowlers in training in order to practise with a reverse-swinging ball Khawaja's allegations have reopened the debate about the sandpaper plot, the investigation into the cheating, the culture of Australian cricket and the reputations of those involved. item.content:encoded: Pat Cummins was named Australia Test captain in 2021 [Getty Images] Australia captain Pat Cummins has hit back at former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims over the sandpaper scandal, calling them "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense". In 2018, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished for a plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town. Khawaja has published his autobiography this week and the former batter has said the entire Australia team, which included Cummins, knew about the sandpaper scheme and should have taken responsibility. But in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in Sydney, Cummins countered and said: "When he says we all knew, if by that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong. "I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening. "He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense." Cummins and Khawaja played 56 Tests together until Khawaja retired from international cricket in January. Khawaja was in the Australia XI when Cummins made his Test debut in 2011 and the pair were also once team-mates in domestic cricket with New South Wales. "Usman is a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations," said Cummins. "In his book he's been casual with my life and the lives of many others - and, I think, Australian cricket. "I support him to tell his story, 100%, I'm glad he feels like he can, but we have to be accountable for the things that we say and do." In a media conference he arranged himself, Cummins began by promising to answer all questions because, he said: "I don't want to talk about this again after today." At times emotional, Cummins addressed a wide range of topics, including: Advice that some of Khawaja's claims are defamatory, but he will not take legal action He had been in contact with Khawaja and Smith since the book was published, but not Warner His belief that the one-year bans handed to Smith and Warner, and a nine-month suspension to Bancroft were "heavy handed" He had no recollection of Australia tampering with the ball in the 2017-18 Ashes series against England He had met with Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg, who has reviewed the files from the original investigation Explaining why sandpaper would have been present in the dressing room and that it was sometimes used by bowlers in training in order to practise with a reverse-swinging ball Khawaja's allegations have reopened the debate about the sandpaper plot, the investigation into the cheating, the culture of Australian cricket and the reputations of those involved. The story has dominated the media in Australia and caused headlines around the cricketing world. Khawaja has been supported by Warner and Chadd Sayers, a seam bowler who was part of the Australia squad on the 2018 tour of South Africa. However, his allegations have been rejected by Darren Lehmann, who was then the Australia head coach and former England batter Graeme Hick, one of Lehmann's assistants. Mitchell Starc, another bowler on the tour, has also denied Khawaja's claims. Khawaja has put a spotlight on Cummins and his fellow bowlers Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon. The four were Australia's attack in Cape Town and remain their first-choice bowlers eight years later. The quartet have always denied any knowledge of the plot, including in the release of a joint-statement in 2021. In his book - Sabr - Khawaja alleged Australia were urged to find ways of getting the ball to swing by a coach, while Bancroft was later encouraged to cheat. Khawaja also said he asked for the entire team to take responsibility for the controversy in Cape Town, but his request was rejected by two unnamed players. Cummins said he does not recall any suggestion that the team should have shared the responsibility, or that it was rejected. On the idea that the whole team were aligned in a plot to tamper with the ball, he said: "There was no masterplan around using illegal methods. People assume you've gone from very legal methods to suddenly taking sandpaper, and there must have been some huge masterplan. "That is not the case. There's no grand plan. There's no team meeting. There's no bowlers saying this is what must happen." "There's big leaps where Usman is being vague." In his book, Khawaja detailed how he was not interviewed as part of the investigation despite sitting next to Bancroft in the changing rooms during the Test at Newlands. Both Khawaja and Warner have criticised the investigation, which Greenberg has said he will not reopen. Cummins confirmed he has met with Greenberg and, although the captain said he did not want to break a "confidence", that Greenberg has reviewed the sandpaper files since the release of Khawaja's book and found the accounts in the investigation to be "consistent". Cummins has played 77 Tests for Australia and has been captain since 2021. He said he has seen only one instance of ball-tampering in his career, during a domestic Sheffield Shield match, when a player took a bottletop on to the field. However, he did admit that balls can sometimes be altered during training sessions, if bowlers want to practise in a certain way, or batters want to face a ball of a particular condition. Cummins said it was not unknown for training balls to be scuffed in such circumstances, using sandpaper or even a Stanley knife. When it was put to Cummins that he, as a bowler, must have suspected that the Cape Town ball had been tampered with, the 33-year-old described that bowlers often touch a ball as little as possible, in order to keep it dry and in a state where it will reverse-swing. At the time of the sandpaper scandal, Cummins was 24 and playing in his 13th Test. Asked about a potential culture of ball-tampering in that era, Cummins said he noticed things then that he now realises could have been cheating. On why Khawaja has chosen to speak now, at the end of his career, rather than in the intervening eight years, Cummins said the episode could have "weighed heavy" on the left-hander. Addressing the culture of the Australia team eight years ago, Cummins said: "I didn't like the way we spoke to umpires, the opposition. I think there was a bit of an arrogance and a bit of an ugliness at times that didn't sit well with me as a young guy. "Now I'm captain, I have spent a lot of time making sure that that's not the case." Speaking about Cummins' news conference on Fox Cricket, where he is working as an analyst for Australia's one-day series against England which got under way on Friday, Warner said: "I stick with Uzzie. It's the truth. The captain threw Uzzie under the bus. "We've got to live with the consequence daily. I feel it was a botched investigation. To get it over and done with. This won't rest. "I'm not going to accept [things] until the truth is out." Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports' Analysis - Cummins did not dodge a single question Khawaja's claims - in his book, in interviews and on social media - have re-opened old wounds in Australian cricket, drawing battle-lines that have verged on civil war. Over the past few days, constant questions have been asked of who knew what and if the truth has been covered up in the intervening eight years. The most pressure has been on the bowlers who played for Australia in Cape Town, none more so than Cummins, given his rise to the captaincy. He has been urged to front up, to show leadership. In an indoor cricket centre in Sydney, Cummins did just that. Others connected to the scandal who have faced the media in the past few days – Lehmann, Starc and Mitchell Marsh – have almost implicated themselves with vague responses to straight questions. Not Cummins. The captain did not duck or dodge any of the su

item.title: "You can't always play the same way for 90 minutes" – Zidane backs Olise after quiet second half against Italy
item.description: "You can't always play the same way for 90 minutes" – Zidane backs Olise after quiet second half against Italy Michael Olise struck early to capitalise on a mistake by Gianluigi Donnarumma and give France the lead in Thursday's UEFA Nations League clash against Italy. However, Olise's influence waned in the second half, as France struggled and ultimately suffered a 3-1 defeat. Speaking after the game, France coach Zinedine Zidane was unconcerned by Olise's drop in performance, arguing it's only natural that the winger cannot always play at the same level. He also pointed to the fact that the 24-year-old has scored five goals in his last five games for the national team. “You can’t always play the same way for 90 minutes. He has scored quite a few goals for us across the last two international breaks, and he has been very good. That’s what I’m focusing on,” Zidane said in defence of Olise at the post-match press conference, via RMC Sport. “I don’t think he was a little less effective in the second half. We were all a little less effective in the second half. And when the team isn’t playing as well, it affects individual performances.” Olise and France will be hoping to finish their UEFA Nations League Group A2 campaign with a win when they face Turkey on Sunday.
