item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. Oregon head coach Dan Lanning talks to the defense during a timeout as the No. 13 Oregon Ducks face the No. 21 UCLA Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. Oregon head coach Dan Lanning talks to the defense during a timeout as the No. 13 Oregon Ducks face the No. 21 UCLA Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian “Everybody knows what we want to attack this next week, being that Nebraska is a good team,” he said. The outside noise has been deafening. To say that many Oregon fans have melted down on social media would be an understatement. Virtually all of the players have social media accounts. Moore said he is active on social media but ignores negativity. Finney said he isn’t very active on social media and doesn’t care what people say outside the program. “Why would I let your opinion inflict me or my thoughts on my performance or my thoughts on our performance,” he said. “Because people are going to be there when you’re doing good, when you’re bad; when you’re doing bad, they’re going to leave you.” For that reason, the team lives by the motto F.E.B.U., which stands for “Forget Everyone But Us”. “F.E.B.U. is a true statement that we all follow,” Finney said. “… Just back to work. We got to figure out what we did wrong, go to the doctor, and just get back to work.” Fifth-year linebacker Devon Jackson said before the season that his main goal was team-driven — winning the national title. He is no longer looking that far ahead. “At the end of the year, what happens, happens, but I promise if we focus on the day and focus on one game at a time, we will be okay,” Jackson said. On Saturday, the Ducks’ defense played one of its best games of the season, while the offense played its worst without starting quarterback Dante Moore , who remains in concussion protocol. On teams that lack closeness, such a contrast can cause issues. But that is not the case with Oregon. “I mean, we’re all in this together,” Jackson said. “It’s not like, the defense won the game and offense lost, or special teams won or lost. We all lost together and we all win together. So, we got each other’s back no matter what.” Oregon offensive players celebrate a touchdown run by running back Jordon Davison (#0) as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 UCLA Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Jackson said that after Saturday’s loss, he and senior center Iapani Laloulu talked for 20 minutes about the team. He told Laloulu that he didn’t care what was going on with the offense; the defense had its back. “I wouldn’t trade that group with anybody else in the country despite what other people may think,” Jackson said. “And we’re going to continue to lean on each other because it’s we all we got and we all we need.” Realistically, Oregon can’t expect much sympathy from outsiders. The Ducks have top-notch facilities, infinite uniform options, a roster with an estimated payroll of $50 million , and a coach who isn’t afraid to speak his mind, as Lanning did after beating the Trojans. Many in the football world certainly wouldn’t mind seeing Oregon fall. “Ain’t nobody going to feel sorry for us,” linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei said. “So just came back in the next day with the mindset ready to work.” . . . item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. Michigan State Spartans defensive back Charles Brantley (4) tackles Illinois Fighting Illini wide receiver Collin Dixon (17) in a Big 10 football game at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, Mich. on Saturday, October 10, 2026. Isaac Ritchey | iritchey@mlive

Isaac Ritchey | iritchey@mlive.com “He knows he’s going to play now,” Lunney told reporters. But so too could Boyd. “We feel like we have another guy on campus in that room that can help us win and we’re very confident in that,” Bielema said. But mostly, Oregon will focus on Illinois’ system. “There might be wrinkles, but very rarely do people change the identity of their offense based on a change of the position,” Lanning said. “So you prepare and then you make sure you have answers for what you think that skill set is.” If Moore doesn’t return this week, Raiola and Thomas will compete for the starting job against Illinois. He led the Ducks from a 14-6 deficit to a win with a four-yard touchdown pass to tight end Jamari Johnson with 28 seconds remaining. Lanning said he’s confident in all four quarterbacks, including sophomore Akili Smith Jr., who had a play package ready for Nebraska if needed. Illinois is most familiar with Raiola, who, as a Nebraska freshman in 2024, passed for 297 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in a 31-24 overtime loss to Illinois. “Raiola is obviously a very accomplished player,” Bielema said. “Kind of almost unusual. You got to almost prepare for possibly three quarterbacks on Saturday. But we’ll kind of handle that during the course of the week and see where that goes.” . . . item.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore ruled out for rest of 2026 season
item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Watch " Oregon Ducks QB Dante Moore to miss remainder of 2026 season " on YouTube Watch The announcement comes days after the reeling Ducks lost 21-10 at Illinois on Saturday in the third straight game Moore missed while in concussion protocol. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt. Saturday’s loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. Without Moore, Oregon scored 42 points over three games and lost twice while rotating between backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. item.content:encoded: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Watch " Oregon Ducks QB Dante Moore to miss remainder of 2026 season " on YouTube Watch The announcement comes days after the reeling Ducks lost 21-10 at Illinois on Saturday in the third straight game Moore missed while in concussion protocol. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt. Saturday’s loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. Without Moore, Oregon scored 42 points over three games and lost twice while rotating between backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Moore was injured on Sept. 26 at USC while sliding to end a 10-yard run to the USC 13-yard line. As Moore began to slide, Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens II hit him in the head with his shoulder. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, center bottom, takes a hard tackle by lSouthern California inebacker Desman Stephens II, center top, during the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill) AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Moore was taken off the field in a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Following Moore’s injury, Raiola entered the game and led the Ducks to a 41-27 win. Moore entered the concussion protocol but returned to practice the following bye week. Speculation was that Moore would return once he cleared the protocols. But each subsequent availability report listed Moore as out. On Oct. 10, Oregon lost 17-15 to UCLA, with Raiola struggling through three quarters before being replaced in the fourth quarter by Thomas. Thomas started the following week against Nebraska, but he played poorly before Raiola entered the game in the fourth quarter and led the Ducks to a 17-14 comeback win. Oregon’s realistic national playoff hopes remained alive at 4-2 — until the loss to Illinois. At 4-3, the Ducks must win their final five games to reach 9-3 and hope enough playoff contenders finish with three losses so the Ducks can receive a berth. If Moore enters the 2027 NFL Draft, his announcement will end his brief Ducks career, during which he led the program to one of its best seasons. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore walks off the field after the No. 5 Ducks fall to the No. 1 Indiana Hoosiers, 56-22, in the Peach Bowl at the College Football Playoff semifinals from Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta on Friday, Jan. 9, 2025. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Lanning said he wasn’t sure what Moore’s plans were after this season. “That’s not fair for me to say or speculate,” Lanning said. “Obviously, he’ll have a decision again at the end of the season and what that looks like. I think we all can acknowledge that Dante is a great player and he will get an opportunity to get drafted. But what that looks like in the future, I think that’s a decision for a later date. I don’t know where his mind is at on that. We haven’t had a conversation. That’s not where my focus is at. I don’t think that’s where his focus is at right now. There’s a reason you get time to make that decision later on.” Moore committed to Oregon in the summer of 2022. Later, he flipped to UCLA in December of 2022 rather than back up Ducks quarterback Bo Nix in 2023. That summer, Moore learned that his mother had been diagnosed with cancer, adding to the pressure he was feeling while trying to perform as a highly touted freshman. Moore had a rough freshman season at UCLA. His midseason struggles led Chip Kelly to bench Moore. Following the season, Moore entered the transfer portal and committed to the Ducks in December 2023. Moore transferred to Oregon to develop while backing up the team’s new starter, Oklahoma transfer Dillon Gabriel. That plan paid off in 2025. Moore passed for 3,565 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions while leading the Ducks to a 13-2 record and the playoff semifinals, where they lost to eventual national champion Indiana. Moore, a projected first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, returned to Oregon for his senior season to keep improving with a team that returned eight defensive starters and was expected to contend for a national championship. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore (#5) celebrates with running back Tradarian Ball (#4) after Ball’s touchdown as the No. 21 Ducks face the Portland State Vikings in a non-conference college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Oregon entered the season ranked No. 2 — the highest preseason ranking in program history — and defeated Boise State, 34-27, in the opener. Moore passed for a career-high 378 yards with three touchdown passes. The season began to unravel the following week when the heavily favored Ducks lost 39-31 at Oklahoma State. The following week, Oregon won 84-0 over Portland State. Next came the USC game. The Ducks, who host No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1), could continue to start Raiola or turn to former four-star recruit Akili Smith Jr. Chances are, Lanning will go with whichever quarterback he believes can win games. In the offseason, Oregon is expected to seek a quarterback in the transfer portal. With high expectations at Oregon, Lanning likely won’t bank on Raiola or Smith as the starter in 2027. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. Oregon Ducks QB Dylan Raiola (8) throws a pass to Oregon Ducks RB Dierre Hill Jr. (6) during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stad
item.content:encoded: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. Oregon Ducks QB Dylan Raiola (8) throws a pass to Oregon Ducks RB Dierre Hill Jr. (6) during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, IL. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire) (Icon Sportswire via AP Images) AP Raiola avoided throwing anyone under the bus but acknowledged what the question implied. Passing games are built on timing. If the quarterback can’t fully trust the receivers running the routes, synergy suffers and efficiency wanes. That’s less a knock on the receivers than an acknowledgment that it’s easier to develop a connection with a team’s more polished top receivers than with those thrust into action by circumstance. At times, running back Dierre Hill Jr. played wide receiver alongside freshmen Hudson Lewis and Gatlin Bair. Neither had played much until injuries hit the group. Lanning said Stewart would return. McClellan is out indefinitely. 5. The failed gadget play Much has been made about the failed gadget play in the third quarter. Many have blamed Mehringer for the play-call and the negative result hurting momentum. Let’s examine. Oregon trailed 14-10, forced an Illinois punt and took over at the Ducks’ 9-yard line. Five plays later, Oregon moved the ball to its 47. That’s when the gadget play came out. Oregon lined up with four offensive linemen to the far left, with wide receiver Dakorien Moore behind the linemen. Three Illinois defenders lined up on that side with a fourth closer to the box. Raiola checked to a run play and handed the ball to Moore on a jet sweep to the right, where the Ducks were outnumbered. The poorly-blocked play resulted in a one-yard loss. A couple of plays later, Oregon punted. After the game, Lanning was asked whether the failed play hurt the team at that moment. “Yeah, it’s a great question,” he said. “It certainly wasn’t successful. There’s a pause in operation there, right?” Yes, but who is at fault for the failed play? Is it Raiola for reading it wrong and not passing to Moore? Is it Mehringer for calling the play? Or is it Lanning for allowing the play to happen? For that play to be called, it must be accepted by Lanning, practiced, reviewed on film and further stamped by Lanning to appear on the play sheet. Then, when Mehringer calls it, Lanning must let it go through. He can hear every play call through the coaches’ headsets. If Lanning didn’t like the play, he could have vetoed it. He did not. The concept is not much different from when Lanning chooses to go for two after touchdowns. If Oregon gets the favorable look it wants, it takes the shot. That’s what happened with the gadget play. But Oregon made the wrong choice and the play failed. Regardless of the process, had Lanning not liked the play, he could have stopped it from being called. 6. Oregon’s rushing attack came to life Oregon gained 180 yards on the ground against a team that ranked 12th in the Big Ten in rushing defense, allowing 134.4 yards per game. CHAMPAIGN, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 24: Jordon Davison #0 of the Oregon Ducks scores a touchdown against Matthew Bailey #7 of Illinois during the first half at Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Champaign, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) Getty Images Still, too many drives started well before getting stuffed, putting more pressure on Raiola, who couldn’t consistently deliver. Tough day for kicker Gage Hurych The junior entered the game 9-for-9 on field-goal attempts and went 1-for-4. But two of his three misses came from beyond 50 yards. Hurych missed his first attempt from 52 yards out. He made a 20-yard field goal in the second quarter to put Oregon up 10-0. He missed a 53-yarder with 6:04 to go in the fourth quarter and later missed a 47-yarder with 52 seconds to go. “He’s human,” Lanning said. “The reality is, those are long kicks. Some of those are really tough. The wind’s a little bit different in this stadium. I think we put them in a position that wasn’t the easiest to operate, and we’ve been really fortunate this year.” 8. Rushing defense faltered when it mattered most. Oregon’s defense kept the Ducks in the games against UCLA and Nebraska until the offense started to come alive. Oregon lost to the Bruins 17-15 and beat Nebraska 17-14. On Saturday, the Ducks led 10-0 late in the second quarter. At that point, nobody knew Oregon wouldn’t score again. But the defense’s job was to keep dominating, just in case. item.content:encoded: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers’ coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game. What style will the Blazers play? In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. The roster is unbalanced, featuring five dynamic ball-handlers and playmakers (Lillard, Morant, Avdija, Holiday and Henderson), a solid center combination (Clingan and Williams) and little wing depth. As a result, the team is expected to play fast and free under Nori, bringing lots of speed, passing, cutting and flow. Nori said he hopes to rotate his players liberally in shorter shifts during games — perhaps as short as three minutes — which will enable them to play with maximum effort before giving way to teammates. The interior defense is strong with Clingan and Williams patrolling the middle, Camara remains one of the NBA’s best and most versatile defenders and Cissoko will be asked to guard one-through-five. Holiday is still capable of locking down opposing guards and Avdija has pledged to be more of a two-way threat now that he doesn’t have to serve as the team’s primary ball-handler. But the backcourt combination of Morant and Lillard, while lethal on offense, is not imposing on defense and relatively small (both stand 6-foot-2). What are the Blazers’ expectations? Portland defied pundits last season, winning 10 of its last 14 regular season games to secure a spot in the play-in tournament, where it beat the Suns in Phoenix to earn the seventh seed in the Western Conference. The San Antonio Spurs dismissed the Blazers with a gentleman’s sweep in the playoffs , but the strong run — combined with the additions of Lillard and Morant — has raised expectations in Portland. How much? Camara said in training camp that the Blazers’ goal is to win 50 or more games and secure home-court advantage in the postseason. It won’t be easy. The league is as deep and talented as ever, and new rules surrounding the lottery should discourage teams from tanking, meaning most of the league will be chasing wins instead of lottery ping-pong balls late into the season. It seemed like a third of the league had given up last year by the All-Star break. Latest Blazers news Joe Freeman’s 3 takeaways from the Trail Blazers’ back-to-back sweep vs. Thunder Trail Blazers lose rotation player for 2 months Joe Freeman’s 3 takeaways from Trail Blazers’ rout over the Thunder Thunder vs. Blazers predictions: Portland looks to snap two-game skid in the first of back-to-back meetings Joe Freeman’s 3 takeaways from Trail Blazers’ lopsided loss to Spurs Early-season schedule is a doozy As the Blazers’ new-look lineup works to build chemistry and a first-year coach settles into a new role, the schedule will be challenging. Six of the first eight games — and 12 of the first 17 — will come on the road and include a slew of playoff contenders, including the Spurs, Oklahoma City Thunder (twice), Minnesota Timberwolves (twice), New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers, Denver Nuggets and Los Angeles Lakers (twice). But what about Dame? The most uplifting part of opening night figures to be the return of Lillard, the franchise icon who is back after spending two seasons in Milwaukee and one season on the injured list. The nine-time All-Star and franchise leader has not played in an NBA regular-season or playoff game since April 27, 2025, when he suffered a torn left Achilles tendon. And he has not played with Portland since March 22, 2023, six months before it traded him to the Bucks. Lillard showed no ill effects from his injury during the exhibition season, when he played in three of the Blazers’ four games and averaged 17.3 points, 2.7 assists and 22.7 minutes. If anything, he looked like the same old Dame, swishing three-pointers, creating off the dribble, initiating offense and drawing defensive attention. Lillard joked earlier this week that he’s “not an old man,” but also acknowledged that he isn’t likely to play upward of 38 minutes a game like he used to and may even take a night off here and there for rest, most likely on a random back-to-back. His addition not only should help cover up two of the Blazers’ biggest weaknesses last season — three-point shooting and shooting in the clutch — but also inspire a thirsty fan base, which has rarely loved a player more. All the while, Lillard says he intends to play with more “joy” than ever. Read the original article on oregonlive.com . Add oregonlive.com as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They’re confident they can challenge any defense vertically. “The underneath throws are going to be there,” Hampton said. “We got the best OC in the country; we’re going to be able to go deep if we want to.” Latest Beavers news Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson going through further testing of hand injury before Boise State game Oregon State basketball lands 3-star center for 2027 class Oregon State wome

item.title: Report: €100m-rated Brighton defender dreams of Real Madrid move despite Liverpool interest
item.description: Report: €100m-rated Brighton defender dreams of Real Madrid move despite Liverpool interest Luka Vuskovic has reportedly identified Real Madrid as his ultimate career destination, potentially complicating Liverpool’s pursuit of the Brighton and Hove Albion defender. According to Sky Sport Germany journalist Florian Plettenberg , Liverpool have placed the 19-year-old on their shortlist for next summer, but the Croatian’s long-term ambition is to play at the Santiago Bernabeu. Vuskovic has made an impressive start to life at Brighton following his move from Tottenham in July. Understandably, his performances have attracted attention across Europe, with the Premier League club now in a strong position to demand a substantial fee for one of its most promising young players. Liverpool interest grows as Vuskovic establishes himself at Brighton Plettenberg reports that Liverpool are monitoring Vuskovic regularly as they assess their defensive options ahead of the summer 2027 transfer window. Luka Vuskovic dreams of playing for Real Madrid one day. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) The centre-back has firmly established himself under Fabian Hurzeler, strengthening his reputation after an impressive loan spell at Hamburger SV. Brighton signed him this past summer for a reported £46 million, with a further £4 million in achievable add-ons. The Croatian agreed a five-year contract running until 2031, and there is no release clause that would allow an interested club to bypass negotiations. Real Madrid are his dream destination Despite Liverpool’s interest, Vuskovic’s long-term ambition is to represent Real Madrid one day. Notably, he is very happy with his development at Brighton, meaning there is no immediate indication that he wants to leave. Liverpool are closely monitoring Luka Vuskovic. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) However, if he does push for an exit, Brighton are understood to value him at around €100 million, a figure that would be a significant increase on their initial investment. Real Madrid will undergo defensive overhaul If Real Madrid are linked with the player in future, it would ideally make sense given their ongoing efforts to build a younger defensive core. Ibrahima Konate joined the club this summer, while Jacobo Ramon has emerged as a possible longer-term option following his development at Como. However, reports suggest Real Madrid have yet to make a final decision on bringing Ramon back. Furthermore, with Antonio Rudiger potentially in his final season, the team will indeed need a new centre-back, leaving Vuskovic as a potentially attractive future target, although the financial implications would be considerable.

item.title: Carlo Ancelotti delivers positive Raphinha update amid Barcelona fitness concerns: ‘Doing very well’
item.description: Carlo Ancelotti delivers positive Raphinha update amid Barcelona fitness concerns: ‘Doing very well’ Carlo Ancelotti has offered an encouraging assessment of Raphinha’s condition ahead of Brazil’s friendly against Japan, confirming that the Barcelona forward is doing well with both club and country. His comments come as Barcelona monitor the winger’s workload during the November international break, with the Catalan club keen to avoid another physical setback after his recent return from injury. Raphinha, who will captain the national team , has travelled to Singapore for Brazil’s two friendlies, against Japan on November 14 and Singapore on November 17. The number of minutes he receives there will be an important consideration for Barcelona, given his value to Hansi Flick and the injuries that have disrupted his recent availability. Ancelotti praises Raphinha’s form and versatility Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Ancelotti offered a positive assessment of the Barcelona forward’s current condition and performances. Raphinha will captain the national team during November friendlies. (Photo by Ian Hitchcock/Getty Images) “Raphinha is doing very well here and at Barcelona. He’s showing impressive quality at Barça and can play as a striker,” said the former Real Madrid boss, according to AS . Raphinha’s fitness remains an important consideration following his recent muscular problems. As stated earlier, Barcelona and the Brazilian Football Confederation have coordinated to manage his involvement during the two friendlies, reducing the risk of another setback. However, it is crucial to note that no specific minutes limit has been publicly confirmed. Meanwhile, Ancelotti also addressed the players’ motivation to represent their country, something that was questioned after Raphinha’s comments during his contract renewal , stressing the importance of Brazil’s status and the support they receive from their fans. Ancelotti confirms Raphinha is motivated to play for Brazil. (Photo by Albert Perez/Getty Images) “I know the players want to play for the national team and I don’t need to say anything to them to get them out there competing. “Brazil is the greatest national team in the world and the fans will be right behind us in every match and will support us. It’s different in other countries.” Flick will be hoping Raphinha returns without another setback For Barcelona, it is quite clear that they will want their captain to complete international duty in good condition. Raphinha’s pressing, attacking output and leadership make him an important part of Flick’s plans, leaving the club with little incentive to take unnecessary risks with his fitness. Brazil, meanwhile, have their own reasons to use him carefully. Ancelotti knows the forward is an important attacking option, and managing his minutes will be crucial even for him, as these two matches are mere friendlies.

item.title: Obi leads NDC supporters in singing old national anthem in Lagos
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), on Thursday joined party supporters in singing Nigeria’s former national anthem, ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’, at a town hall meeting in Lagos. Obi, alongside Funso Doherty, the party’s governorship candidate in Lagos State, and other attendees, declined to stand for the recital of the current national anthem when prompted by the event anchor. The anchor subsequently switched to the old anthem, which Obi and the supporters sang together. During the recital, Obi faced the crowd with two fingers raised on both hands, forming a gesture associated with the NDC logo. A video of the incident, which has since circulated on social media, showed the party supporters enthusiastically singing the former national anthem. The development comes amid controversy surrounding the reintroduction of the old anthem by President Bola Tinubu. On May 29, 2024, Tinubu signed the National Anthem Bill into law, restoring ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’ as the country’s official anthem, replacing ‘Arise, O Compatriots’. The old anthem was first adopted at Nigeria’s independence on October 1, 1960, and remained in use until 1978, when it was replaced. Meanwhile, the town hall meeting was earlier disrupted when suspected thugs reportedly invaded the venue with cutlasses, cudgels and stones, forcing attendees to flee for safety. Obi previously secured victory in Lagos State during the 2023 presidential election as the Labour Party candidate, polling 582,354 votes against Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who received 572,606 votes. The post Obi leads NDC supporters in singing old national anthem in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Record-breaking Harry Kane sees Luka Modrić’s career as an inspiration
item.description: England fans hold up a tifo featuring England's Harry Kane, marking his Ballon d'Or triumph and his achievement in becoming England's all-time record appearance holder with 126 appearances, ahead of the UEFA Nations League match between England vs Croatia at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «Record-breaking Harry Kane sees Luka Modrić’s career as an inspiration») John Walton/PA Wire/dpa Harry Kane vowed to “push the limits” like inspirational 41-year-old Luka Modrić following his record-breaking England appearance against Croatia. The 33-year-old enjoyed a night to remember at a sold-out Wembley on Thursday, when a giant tifo hailed ‘England’s finest’ as the captain led the team for his landmark 126th cap. Kane was given a rapturous reception and displayed the Ballon d’Or to the crowd before a series of presentations centred on him setting a new England’s men’s appearance record. The Prince of Wales, William, and previous record holder Peter Shilton led the celebrations on a night that ended with the skipper’s spot-kick sealing a 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia under the arch. “It was incredible, just everything was amazing,” said Kane, who admitted he was “trying to play it cool” when he walked out to see a giant banner recognizing his 126th cap. “A big thank you to everyone who organized it here at the FA, with the tifo and presentations. Thank you to Luka (Modrić) and the Croatian organization for their gift as well. “Obviously I knew there was going to be something before the game and it was just a special moment. “It’s been a crazy few weeks with a lot happening and of course it’s an important moment in our history as a national team, so you have to enjoy these moments. “But then once the game started, it was just full focus on that. “I’ve said before, these occasions feel much better when you win and obviously now I can take a breath and enjoy the whole night itself.” Kane was on the Wembley pitch long after the final whistle with friends and family, who will have undoubtedly further significant moments to celebrate in the years to come. The striker is now just eight international goals shy of joining the 100 club and plans to play for England until the wheels come off, with fellow Ballon d’Or winner Modrić's longevity providing motivation. (is associated with: «Record-breaking Harry Kane sees Luka Modrić’s career as an inspiration») John Walton/PA Wire/dpa Harry Kane vowed to “push the limits” like inspirational 41-year-old Luka Modrić following his record-breaking England appearance against Croatia. The 33-year-old enjoyed a night to remember at a sold-out Wembley on Thursday, when a giant tifo hailed ‘England’s finest’ as the captain led the team for his landmark 126th cap. Kane was given a rapturous reception and displayed the Ballon d’Or to the crowd before a series of presentations centred on him setting a new England’s men’s appearance record. The Prince of Wales, William, and previous record holder Peter Shilton led the celebrations on a night that ended with the skipper’s spot-kick sealing a 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia under the arch. “It was incredible, just everything was amazing,” said Kane, who admitted he was “trying to play it cool” when he walked out to see a giant banner recognizing his 126th cap. “A big thank you to everyone who organized it here at the FA, with the tifo and presentations. Thank you to Luka (Modrić) and the Croatian organization for their gift as well. “Obviously I knew there was going to be something before the game and it was just a special moment. “It’s been a crazy few weeks with a lot happening and of course it’s an important moment in our history as a national team, so you have to enjoy these moments. “But then once the game started, it was just full focus on that. “I’ve said before, these occasions feel much better when you win and obviously now I can take a breath and enjoy the whole night itself.” Kane was on the Wembley pitch long after the final whistle with friends and family, who will have undoubtedly further significant moments to celebrate in the years to come. The striker is now just eight international goals shy of joining the 100 club and plans to play for England until the wheels come off, with fellow Ballon d’Or winner Modrić's longevity providing motivation. The 41-year-old extended his Croatian appearance record to 207 after coming off the bench at Wembley, where England fans gave him a warm reception. “He’s an inspiration for a lot of us,” Kane said. “What an incredible player, but what a great person as well and someone who’s looked after himself. “A great professional and to be playing 40, 41 now, still at this level, is credit to all of his hard work and his mentality. “So, yeah, that inspires me to push the limits. Like with him, I think you just keep going to see how far your body takes you, your mentality takes you. “Everyone’s journey is different for sure but I’ve said before that as long as I feel like I can help the national team, as long as I feel like I’m performing at the highest level, then I’ll be here for as long as I can. “Whether that’s until I’m 40 or not, we’ll have to wait and see. But right now, yeah, I’ve enjoyed every moment.” Kane’s immediate attention is on England’s final fixture of the year against World Cup winners Spain in Madrid, where they head having rubberstamped progress to the Nations League quarter-finals. Thomas Tuchel’s side lost 3-2 to Wembley in the Group A3 opener but four straight wins since then gives them hope of finishing top of the pool on Sunday. “There were things that we can improve on, but it was just about getting the win ultimately,” Kane added. “It sets up a fantastic game on Sunday now.”

item.title: Coco Gauff Clears The Air About ‘Stupid’ WTA Finals Rules Complaint After Backlash
item.description: Coco Gauff. © IMAGN Coco Gauff addressed the backlash surrounding her recent comments about the WTA Finals format. Gauff started her run in Indian Wells with a 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-2 win over compatriot Jessica Pegula. However, she fell in the next round to Linda Noskova, who beat her 6-3, 6-3. The defeat made her advancement in the semifinal round uncertain. Her qualification not only depended on her match against Marta Kostyuk, but also on Pegula’s clash against Linda Noskova. After her second loss, Gauff appeared to express frustration with WTA qualification. Later, following her third-round match against Kostyuk, she was asked to address her previous statement. Gauff clarified that she wasn’t calling the format stupid; rather, she meant that thinking about different qualification scenarios while playing a match would be foolish. “Can I clear that up? Okay. I wasn’t saying the format was stupid. I was saying if you get in if you get like in your head while you’re playing into all the scenarios that’s stupid. But of course, everyone thought I was calling the format [laughter] stupid. But I was trying to because he asked me, ‘Am I gonna look at the different scenarios and stuff,’ and I was trying to say like no, if I like play while thinking about the scenarios it’s stupid because it’s tennis. Like you can’t, ‘Oh, I want to win this match in straight sets.’ Every match you want to win in straight sets.” Despite seeing off Marta Kostyuk, Coco Gauff saw her pursuit come to an end as Jessica Pegula finished in second place in Group 1 after dominating Linda Noskova 7-6(2), 4-6, 7-5. Coco Gauff opens up about the hot mic controversy at the WTA Finals involving her, Mirra Andreeva and Jessica Pegula Coco Gauff recently opened up about the hot mic incident at the WTA Finals, where Jessica Pegula was heard making statements about her compatriot and Mirra Andreeva. Pegula slammed Andreeva, calling her a ‘diva’ who ‘needed to be humbled.’ She also criticized Andreeva’s coach, Conchita Martinez, for putting up with her behavior. Pegula also compared Andreeva and Gauff, saying Andreeva could be a better player and surpass Gauff if she had Gauff’s mentality. During the event, Gauff addressed the incident, stating that she had no grudges with Pegula. “Jess, she told me, before I even saw the video, she came and apologized immediately,” Gauff said. “Honestly, I didn’t really take it. I feel like maybe the other person in the situation got a lot more of it. But she, you know, they both, even her coach, apologized to me. So yeah, I think for me, I’m a competitor, so I’m always going to compete regardless of what’s happening off the court. But yeah, I know her heart, and it was all good. I don’t feel any type of way.” Jessica Pegula will lock horns with Mirra Andreeva in the semifinals of the WTA Finals. item.title: Chicago Bears Win Despite Historic Mess Against Tampa Bay
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears made history on Sunday night by winning a game despite committing five turnovers, taking nine penalties, and failing to rush for a single 10‑yard gain. Yahoo Sports noted this odd mix of errors and victory makes the team look different than any other squad in the league this season. No other team in NFL history has ever blown a 14-point lead at home, taken so many penalties, and still secured a win against a team like Tampa Bay. Bears head coach Ben Johnson admitted the team did not play their best football during the 27-24 victory over the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 8. He told reporters that while the win is what matters most right now, the style of play leaves room for growth. “At the end of the day, that’s the end goal that we’re looking for,” Johnson said, referring to the victory itself. He also noted that the players in the locker room knew they had underperformed even though they got the win. A Team Finding Its Grit Johnson felt a specific energy from the group despite the sloppy stats, which he called a positive sign for the future. “I felt that from our crew, which is a good thing,” Johnson said. The team now sits at 7-2 as they head into their bye week, giving them time to fix the issues that plagued them against Tampa Bay. The coach said good teams can win without playing their A‑game. Key players like linebacker Devin Bush and edge rusher Austin Booker stepped up when the offense struggled to move the ball. Johnson commended Bush for delivering a top-tier performance as a Chicago Bear, a sight that was remarkable. He further emphasized Booker’s intensity and effort, observing that the defensive players continue improving week in and week out. These individual efforts helped the team overcome the five turnovers and the loss of a 14-point lead. Health and Rest Are Next The bye week offers a crucial chance for the roster to heal up before the final stretch of the season. Several key players, including running back Kyle Monangai and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, have missed games this year and need this time to recover. Quarterback Caleb Williams also gets a week to rest his hamstring, while wide receiver Luther Burden III uses the time to recover from a concussion suffered in the game. Yahoo Sports reported that the power rankings have shifted dramatically at the midway point of the season, with only half of the preseason top 10 teams remaining in the top 10. The Bears have moved into a strong position, but the coach says the team still needs to improve its play to reach its full potential. Johnson said the team needs to continue evolving so they can win in the right manner, not just by luck or grit alone. The team will use this week to review the first nine games and decide what areas need the most work before the season ends.

item.title: Hawks Are Hot, But The Eastern Conference Reality Check Is Here
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Atlanta Hawks are sitting pretty at 7-5, but that record might be a bit of a mirage. Monday’s loss to the Los Angeles Lakers ended their four-game winning streak, placing them fourth in the Eastern Conference. The team has had a solid start, yet the gap between looking good and being a real contender is wide. Sports Illustrated notes that the Hawks have played more games than any other league team so far, indicating a brutal schedule. Staying in the upper echelon of the East currently requires winning against bad teams. With a combined 2-20 record, the Chicago Bulls and Milwaukee Bucks rank as two of the worst NBA teams. If the Hawks drop games against these bottom-tier squads, they will fall fast. To keep pace, Atlanta must take care of business against the worst of the bunch. Dyson Daniels Is The Only True Star While the offense can be shaky, Dyson Daniels is doing something special on both ends of the floor. Although Jalen Johnson receives more hype, he is arguably Atlanta’s most impactful player right now. Daniels just posted 10 points, eight rebounds, and six assists against the Lakers, along with four steals. For the whole season, he holds a team-best plus-58 rating when he is on the court. He is the Hawks’ best defender, and without him, the mediocre defense would be much worse. As the team prepares to face Chicago, he demonstrates high-level play as one of the NBA’s most underrated impact players. Julius Okongwu has posted 16 or more points in each of his last three outings and recorded nine rebounds in four of his last five contests. He has a plus-38 rating in his minutes. Lu Dort And The Backup Center Problem Not everyone is playing well, and Lu Dort is the biggest concern for the coaching staff. It has not been a great season for him in Atlanta, and the loss to the Lakers showed why. Dort scored only four points and shot 1-for-6 from three against the Lakers. He is a minus-38 in his minutes, the lowest on the entire team. When he does not shoot well, his defense is not good enough to justify the heavy minutes he is getting. The center position is another headache. Jock Landale returned from injury but played only 14 minutes against the Lakers and finished with five points. It was a questionable move to play him over rookie Zuby Ejiofor, who only played 3:52. Landale was not exceptional in his time, and the backup minutes remain a puzzle for Quin Snyder. According to reports, the Hawks rank 16th in points allowed per 100 possessions, marking them as a middle-of-the-pack defense. If they lose to Chicago or Milwaukee, it will be because they could not stop the other team’s offense. Friday night will see the Hawks resume play on the road against the Chicago Bulls.

item.title: Rangers Eye Sato But Phillies Could Land Power Hitter First
item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images The Texas Rangers are showing interest in Japanese star Teruaki Sato, but a deal there looks like a long shot. According to Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic, the club is just one of several teams watching the market. The Phillies are also among the suitors, which puts Philadelphia in a prime spot to make a move if the price stays reasonable. This year’s free agent class likely features Sato as the premier position player, and his power bat might solve a lineup requiring more punch. Texas has bigger financial headaches than a new outfielder right now. The club is focused on shedding obligations to stars like Corey Seager, Jacob deGrom, and Nathan Eovaldi. MLB Trade Rumors predicted Sato would sign a five-year, $80 million deal, but other public estimates put the value well into the nine-figure range. The signing team also has to pay a posting fee based on that contract value. With the Rangers ending the 2026 season with a $218.7 million luxury tax number, spending big on Sato seems unlikely given their current payroll constraints. Power Comes With Strikeout Risks This year, Sato has hit 39 home runs for the Hashin Tigers, generating immense power from the left side. Across 614 plate appearances, he followed that performance with a .306/.383/.609 slash line. However, evaluators have questions about his pure hitting ability against better pitching. In a league where pitcher quality falls below Major League Baseball standards, he struck out at a 26.7 percent rate. Sato has a decent chance of punching out 30 percent of the time in the big leagues. Teams might accept those whiffs if he keeps hitting 30 or more homers, but it is a risky bet. Fit In Texas Or Philly While Sato has primarily played third base in Japan, numerous scouts believe he is better suited for a corner outfield role in the majors. Josh Jung secures the hot corner for Texas, but the team faces a vacancy at designated hitter as Joc Pederson explores free agency. They could also sign a left fielder while designating Wyatt Langford as the everyday center fielder. The Phillies need a left-handed bat to balance their lineup, and Sato fits that need perfectly. If the Rangers pull back due to cost, Philadelphia could swoop in to grab a player who hit 40 homers just one season ago. An estimated $192.8 million cash payroll and a $218.7 million luxury tax number marked the end of the 2026 season for the Rangers.

item.title: 49ers’ Fred Warner Sparks Blunt Words From Cowboys’ Dak Prescott
item.description: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers defense will be looking to make life challenging for the Dallas Cowboys‘ offense. San Francisco’s defense will be looking to carry over their defensive performance in Week 9 against the Las Vegas Raiders into this game. Against the Raiders, the Niners’ defense recorded five takeaways, including three interceptions and two forced fumbles. Fred Warner was one of the players who recorded a takeaway against the Silver and Black. Ahead of the game against the 49ers, Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott shared his thoughts on facing Warner. Their offensive unit will have to account for where the linebacker is on the field and will need to hold on tight to the football, as Warner will be there to try to punch it out. “He’s probably the best linebacker in the NFL right now,” Prescott told reporters on Nov. 1 2. “The way he plays the game mentally, reading the splits, reading the back, whether he’s near or far, and making his different calls is impressive. “Their defense is simple because he can get them into the right positions. They play fast, and they play hard. There’s a little bit of a chess match there, but it’s no different from play callers calling the plays. At the end of the day, it’s about execution.” Warner has played 502 total snaps for the 49ers defense so far this season, leading to an 86.2 overall PFF defensive grade . Moreover, the veteran linebacker has recorded 54 solo tackles, generated five total pressures, one sack, 29 stops, and allowed an 84.6 passer rating when targeted in coverage. 49ers’ Fred Warner Draws More Praise From Cowboys Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown won’t be on the field at the same time as Warner, but the Dallas linebacker has a lot of respect for the 49ers star. “I have the utmost respect for him,” Overshown told reporters on Nov. 12 . “Since he came into this league, he’s been a dog. He’s been somebody you have to scout during the week. You have to know where 54 is and be aware when you’re carrying the ball. He’s the prototype linebacker. When you want to come into this league and be a great linebacker, you look at 54. “You look at Fred and what he’s done to change the game, especially how the linebacker position is played from sideline to sideline. I’d like to say he opened the doors for guys like me with my body type to come in and play four downs of football. I have the utmost respect for him. It’s going to be good watching him play, but it’s a battle at the end of the day. We want to come out as the linebacker unit that showed up and made the plays.” Fred Warner Gets Blunt on Facing Dallas’ Offense Meanwhile, Warner has plenty of respect for the Cowboys offense. item.content:encoded: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers defense will be looking to make life challenging for the Dallas Cowboys‘ offense. San Francisco’s defense will be looking to carry over their defensive performance in Week 9 against the Las Vegas Raiders into this game. Against the Raiders, the Niners’ defense recorded five takeaways, including three interceptions and two forced fumbles. Fred Warner was one of the players who recorded a takeaway against the Silver and Black. Ahead of the game against the 49ers, Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott shared his thoughts on facing Warner. Their offensive unit will have to account for where the linebacker is on the field and will need to hold on tight to the football, as Warner will be there to try to punch it out. “He’s probably the best linebacker in the NFL right now,” Prescott told reporters on Nov. 1 2. “The way he plays the game mentally, reading the splits, reading the back, whether he’s near or far, and making his different calls is impressive. “Their defense is simple because he can get them into the right positions. They play fast, and they play hard. There’s a little bit of a chess match there, but it’s no different from play callers calling the plays. At the end of the day, it’s about execution.” Warner has played 502 total snaps for the 49ers defense so far this season, leading to an 86.2 overall PFF defensive grade . Moreover, the veteran linebacker has recorded 54 solo tackles, generated five total pressures, one sack, 29 stops, and allowed an 84.6 passer rating when targeted in coverage. 49ers’ Fred Warner Draws More Praise From Cowboys Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown won’t be on the field at the same time as Warner, but the Dallas linebacker has a lot of respect for the 49ers star. “I have the utmost respect for him,” Overshown told reporters on Nov. 12 . “Since he came into this league, he’s been a dog. He’s been somebody you have to scout during the week. You have to know where 54 is and be aware when you’re carrying the ball. He’s the prototype linebacker. When you want to come into this league and be a great linebacker, you look at 54. “You look at Fred and what he’s done to change the game, especially how the linebacker position is played from sideline to sideline. I’d like to say he opened the doors for guys like me with my body type to come in and play four downs of football. I have the utmost respect for him. It’s going to be good watching him play, but it’s a battle at the end of the day. We want to come out as the linebacker unit that showed up and made the plays.” Fred Warner Gets Blunt on Facing Dallas’ Offense Meanwhile, Warner has plenty of respect for the Cowboys offense. On Nov. 11, the veteran linebacker spoke to the media and talked about Dallas’ offense, as they’ll be looking to make that unit’s life difficult in this contest. Warner noted that the 49ers need to be on their A-game, given that the Cowboys can hurt them in the passing game. “Dak [Prescott has] always played at a high level at the quarterback position,” Warner told reporters . “A guy I got a ton of respect for as a player and as a leader for their team. He has some really elite weapons on the outside. “CeeDee [Lamb] is having a tremendous year, getting a lot of targets, but also making use of those targets. George Pickens is also a huge weapon and has freakish ability when he gets the ball in his hands.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post 49ers’ Fred Warner Sparks Blunt Words From Cowboys’ Dak Prescott appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: SEC Football Week 11 Predictions: Picks for Every Game
item.description: There’s no hard and fast rule that the College Football Playoff can’t pick an at-large 9-3 team over a 10-2 team from a Power Four conference, but it’s never happened before. You’re on your own if you want to risk it. However, several SEC teams will be in CFP mix even with a third loss, but the freakout will come if Alabama, Texas, Tennessee, and/or Kentucky get that third hit. Even worse, it’s over if any of the three-loss teams – South Carolina, LSU, Ole Miss, or Missouri – lose. Here are our quick previews and predictions for every SEC game. – Predictions: ACC | Big Ten SEC Week 11 Previews, Predictions Nov 7, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Kentucky Wildcats quarterback Kenny Minchey (3) calls a play at the line of scrimmage against the Tennessee Volunteers during the first quarter at Neyland Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images SEC Week 11 Quick Hits Texas at LSU is the highest-profile SEC game of the week, but Missouri at Georgia could become a 2026 season-changer if the Tigers come up with something big. It’s a dangerous week for Alabama and Tennessee, going on the road to deal with desperate Mississippi State and Vanderbilt teams, respectively. The pressure will mostly be on Kentucky. It dropped big in the CFP after loss to Tennessee, and it can’t afford a loss to Florida. Jump to Each Quick Preview – Auburn at Mississippi State – Alabama at Vanderbilt – Tennessee at Texas A&M – Ole Miss at Oklahoma – Florida at Kentucky – South Carolina at Arkansas Auburn at Mississippi State: Can the Tigers Avoid the Bulldog Trap Game? Game Time: 12:00 PM ET | TV: ESPN2 Location: Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville, MS The best thing to happen to Mississippi State during a five-game losing streak is the announced signing and return of star quarterback Kamario Taylor for next year. The Bulldog defense has been great, but the offense isn’t moving well enough to push past a decent D. Auburn might be working too hard, but the defensive front is great at getting into the backfield and should come up with just enough big stops late to hold off a late Bulldog rally in a terrific game. Prediction: Auburn 27, Mississippi State 24 Consensus Line: Auburn -2.5, o/u: 50.5 ATS Confidence: 3 | Must See: 3 Alabama at Vanderbilt: Letdown Alert For the Crimson Tide Game Time: 12:45 PM ET | TV: SEC Network Location: FirstBank Stadium, Nashville, TN No. 3 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, Alabama has love from the committee, and now it just has to finish the drill with Chattanooga and Auburn to close. First, it has to take down a Vanderbilt team that finally came up with its first SEC win of the season, beating Mississippi State 25-23. Alabama might not be its sharpest out of the gate – a hangover effect from the 31-13 win at LSU – but just when it seems like this might be interesting, the Commodore turnovers will come. Bama will convert off all three turnovers it generates. Prediction: Alabama 37, Vanderbilt 17 Consensus Line: Alabama -18.5, o/u

Prediction: Alabama 37, Vanderbilt 17 Consensus Line: Alabama -18.5, o/u: 50.5 ATS Confidence: 3 | Must See: 2.5 Tennessee at Texas A&M: The Volunteer Gauntlet Continues Game Time: 3:00 PM ET | TV: ESPN Location: Kyle Field, College Station, TX Over the last few years, SEC fans have liked to use the word gauntlet when it comes to some teams’ tough schedules. In Tennessee’s case, the term applies, facing Alabama (CFP No. 3), South Carolina (CFP No. 17), and Kentucky (CFP No. 11) in the last three games, and with LSU up next after what qualifies as a week off at Texas A&M. The Aggies have been brutally close to finally pulling off something meaningful, but it’s 1-5 in the SEC after a heartbreaking loss at South Carolina. The defense that can’t generate a sack will have a hard time on third downs, but it’ll be a tough effort at home that comes just short against a Volunteer defense that continues to take the ball away in bunches. Prediction: Tennessee 24, Texas A&M 20 Consensus Line: Tennessee -2.5, o/u: 44.5 ATS Confidence: 2 | Must See: 3.5 Missouri at Georgia Game Time: 3:30 PM ET | TV: ABC Location: Sanford Stadium, Athens, GA Prediction: Full CFN Game Preview and Prediction Consensus Line: Georgia -14.5, o/u: 47 Ole Miss at Oklahoma: Will the Rebels Get Their Groove Back? Game Time: 4:15 PM ET | TV: SEC Network Location: Memorial Stadium, Norman, OK There’s nothing like seeing Georgia run out of the tunnel in your ballpark and watching it conduct a light scrimmage. Ole Miss didn’t have any answers in a 42-7 loss to the CFP No. 1 team last week, and now it has to go on a roll to have any prayer of being considered for a high ranking by the playoff committee. Oklahoma continues its schizophrenic season, following every win with a loss. The defense was brilliant in a 23-7 win over Florida, but it won’t have the same luck against an Ole Miss offense that needs to stop turning the ball over. Star Rebel running back Kewan Lacy is out for the season, but Trinidad Chambliss will bounce back from his rough day against the Bulldogs with a sharp day. Too many decent Oklahoma drives will end up with field goals. Prediction: Ole Miss 23, Oklahoma 19 Consensus Line: Oklahoma -1.5, o/u: 49.5 ATS Confidence: 2.5 | Must See: 3.5 Florida at Kentucky: Can the Wildcats Stay in the CFP Chase? Game Time: 6:15 PM ET | TV: ESPN Location: Kroger Field, Lexington, KY CFP No. 11 Kentucky is still 7-2, with a playoff spot almost certainly for the taking if it can beat Missouri and Louisville. It has to get past the ugly 34-6 loss to Tennessee last week and keep its Florida groove going. The Wildcats have won four of the last five in the series. Before that, the Gators went 32-1 going back to 1986. It’s all about the ground game with the Gators. They’re 5-0 when running for over 120 yards, and 0-4 when running for that many or fewer. Kentucky got rumbled over by Tennessee, South Carolina, and Alabama. It’s about to get hit by a good day from the Gators as they rebound big after last week. Prediction: Florida 28, Kentucky 24 Consensus Line: Kentucky -3.5, o/u: 52.5 ATS Confidence: 1.5 | Must See: 4 Texas at LSU Game Time: 7:30 PM ET | TV: ABC Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA Prediction: Full CFN Game Preview and Prediction Consensus Line: LSU -4.5, o/u: 46.5 South Carolina at Arkansas: Shhhhhh, the Gamecocks Are In This Game Time: 7:45 PM ET | TV: SEC Network Location: Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville, AR Don’t get totally caught up in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. Soon, there will be big arguments about several three-loss teams and how worthy they might be. South Carolina started 2-3, but it’s rolling with a four-game winning streak. That’s not why the CFP No. 17 team has reason to dream of finishing in the top 12. Next week? Georgia. Beat the No. 1 team, drop Clemson, and all of a sudden, there will be a discussion. First, it has to get by a plucky Arkansas team that’s far better than the 3-6 record might indicate. Nothing comes easy for the Gamecocks. Star quarterback LaNorris Sellers is banged up, but he’s expected to go. Fortunately for 16, Arkansas doesn’t have a pass rush to get to him. As long as Sellers is sniffing around a 65% completion rate, the Gamecocks will get through another grind of a game, and then it’s on to the Bulldogs. Prediction: South Carolina 26, Arkansas 17 Consensus Line: South Carolina -7.5, o/u: 51.5 ATS Confidence: 3 | Must See: 3 Consensus line based on BetMGM, Caesars, DraftKings, and FanDuel.
