item.title: Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest battle Newcastle for highly-rated Santos starlet eyed by Bayern Munich
item.description: Santos v Palmeiras - Brasileirao 2026 - Getty Images Sport Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest are leading the Premier League chase to sign highly-rated Santos midfielder Gabriel Bontempo during the January transfer window. The English duo face stiff competition from Newcastle United for the 21-year-old Brazilian, who also attracted an enquiry from Bayern Munich over the summer. English clubs target Brazilian prospect According to TEAMtalk , the race for Bontempo is gathering pace as top-flight recruitment teams prepare mid-season approaches for one of South America's most sought-after emerging talents. Capable of operating effectively across several midfield and attacking roles, the versatile playmaker has developed rapidly at domestic level over recent months. His progress was recently rewarded with a senior international call-up to Carlo Ancelotti's latest Brazil squad . Scouting networks drive winter interest The report states that Forest's acclaimed South American scouting network is strongly pushing the City Ground hierarchy to explore a formal move for the youngster ahead of the New Year. Recruitment chiefs in the East Midlands have already built a strong reputation for identifying talent in the region after their groundwork helped bring Murillo, Jair Cunha and Igor Jesus to the club's attention. Meanwhile, the Cherries have emerged as serious contenders after lodging their own enquiries as they assess midfield options in case Alex Scott moves on. Having already demonstrated their willingness to recruit directly from the Brazilian market by signing Rayan last January, the south-coast outfit are keen to explore another deal in the country this winter. European heavyweights join growing queue Up on Tyneside, sporting director Ross Wilson and newly appointed head of recruitment Tomas Amaral are also monitoring the situation closely as they evaluate long-term additions. Both executives possess extensive knowledge of the South American market, while fellow English top-flight sides Brighton & Hove Albion and Brentford have also made initial enquiries as they track emerging prospects in Brazil. Beyond the Premier League, insiders note that clubs across Italy, Spain and Germany are keeping tabs on his trajectory after the Bavarian giants asked about his situation during the summer window. That widespread continental interest underlines the fierce competition for his signature and ensures the Vila Belmiro hierarchy will face mounting pressure over the coming months. Long contract strengthens negotiating stance Despite the growing clamour from overseas suitors, Santos hold a commanding position ahead of the January market as Bontempo remains tied to the club until 2030. The Brazilian side have no intention of allowing one of their brightest stars to depart on the cheap and will demand a substantial financial package before considering any approach. item.title: Ireland bounce back to beat UAE in Emerging Nations
item.description: Ireland secured a comfortable 61-run victory [Getty Images] Second T20 international, Ajman Ireland Women 171-5 (20 overs): Lewis 71, Maritz 29; Thirukkumaran 2-20 United Arab Emirates Women 110-8 (20 overs): Oza 51, Dharnidharka 18; Murray 2-21 Ireland Women win by 61 runs Scorecard Ireland Women recovered from their opening Emerging Nations Trophy defeat by Sri Lanka to claim a comfortable 61-run victory against United Arab Emirates in their second game in Ajman. The UAE won the toss and elected to field first, with Lloyd Tennant's side producing a much stronger showing with the bat than they did against Sri Lanka. The opening partnership of vice-captain Amy Hunter and captain Gaby Lewis laid the foundations for the Irish. Hunter managed 29 runs from 27 balls before she was run out by Suraksha Kotte, while Lewis finished as Ireland's top run scorer with 71, including 12 fours and a six before she was dismissed by Indhuja Nandakumar in the 12th over. Janani Thirukkumaran then forced out Louise Little (seven) in the next over and claimed her second wicket from Lara Maritz soon after, although she did add 29 to Ireland's tally from just 23 balls. Laura Delany was 18 not out while Theertha Satish ran out Alana Dazell (11) as Ireland finished on 171-5 from their 20 overs. The UAE had a nightmare start to their response as they lost Satish, Heena Hotchandhani and Rinitha Rajith all inside the first two overs. Samaira Dharnidharka added 18 to the tally before becoming the fourth player to exit when she was bowled out by Cara Murray in the seventh over. Esha Oza steadied the ship as she registered 51 runs from 45 balls with five fours and a six before being dismissed by Little. The wickets continued to tumble as Thirukkumaran (13), Mehul Kulkarni (six) and Athige Sashikala Silva (four) all went as UAE fell well short of the target, ending with 110-8. Ireland will next be in action on Monday when they face face Papua New Guinea (09:15 GMT) before rounding off their group campaign with a game against Scotland on Wednesday, 18 November (05:00 GMT).

item.title: ‘This break came at the ideal moment for me’: Senne Lammens happy to escape Manchester United crisis for a week of international football
item.description: ‘This break came at the ideal moment for me’: Senne Lammens happy to escape Manchester United crisis for a week of international football It is fair to say that Senne Lammens has not been enjoying the best of times at Manchester United in the past few weeks. However, on Thursday evening Lammens was able to escape the crisis that has been engulfing Manchester United in recent weeks and join up with the Belgian national team . Despite his dip in form at club level, Mark van Bommel stuck with Lammens in goal against Türkiye as Belgium won 2-1 away from home. Speaking to the media after the game, Lammens reflected on what has been a tough time in Manchester. The goalkeeper said ‘ This break came at the ideal moment for me ‘. There had been some rumours that perhaps van Bommel would opt for a different goalkeeper, with Mike Penders having done well for Chelsea in recent weeks. However, the former Antwerp head coach stuck with Lammens and the Manchester United goalkeeper made a number of saves to ensure Belgium took all three points. Lammens felt good after the game, before also saying ‘ These have been difficult weeks for me at Manchester United ‘. On his return to his club after the break, Lammens will be operating under a new head coach. With Michael Carrick gone, the 24-year-old will be looking to impress the new head coach, which looks to be Mauricio Pochettino. Lammens did speak about Carrick’s departure, saying ‘ The team really did support the manager, but when the results don’t follow, you know this can happen. We know that we have to do much better ‘. GBeNeFN | Ben Jackson

item.title: England thrashed by Australia in first ODI to provide welcome distraction to sandpaper scandal
item.description: England crashed to a heavy defeat in the first game of their latest Australian tour, with a rousing debut from 21-year-old Mahli Beardman diverting some of the home side’s attention from the ongoing sandpaper scandal . Australian cricket is in the midst of a bitter civil war over Usman Khawaja’s historic ball-tampering allegations but the hosts still eased to a seven-wicket victory in in the first ODI in Perth , where local boy Beardman collected stunning figures of six for 24. It proved another calamitous visit to Optus Stadium for England, who thew away the first Ashes Test in two days on the same ground 12 months ago. With Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood all rested between Test series, Australia pieced together an inexperienced attack and watched as it dismantled their rivals. At one stage England were 65 for eight and staring at a record low total, with some late repair work by the tail lifting them to 131 all out. Travis Head missed the chance to repeat his match-winning Ashes knock when he was bowled cheaply by Gus Atkinson but skipper Mitch Marsh took up the mantle, clubbing 50 off just 30 balls to lead a chase that was all over in less than 24 overs. England were criticised last winter for being too casual in their preparations Down Under but that has not been the case this time. They have trained hard, given themselves time to acclimatise and beaten Western Australia in a warm-up game at the WACA. All of that work came to nothing, though, as they followed up a disappointing tri-series in Pakistan with a fourth loss in their last five outings. After being sent in England’s openers scraped together 24 before Australia bagged their first, Ben Duckett slashing Spencer Johnson to backward point. Ben Duckett was the first English batsman to get out (AP) Tom Banton came closer than anyone to finding form, hitting five fours on his way to 25 before driving with hard hands at the tidy Xavier Bartlett. An average start then transformed into a dreadful once as the introduction of Beardman plunged the innings into turmoil. Kicking off his senior international career with England’s two best batters at the crease, the youngster got the best of both. His eighth ball was sharp and well directed, with enough swing to take the outside edge as Harry Brook went back in defence. Joe Root , on the day he became just the third Englishman to 200 ODI appearances, was even bigger scalp. Muddling his way to 17 from 36 balls, he was put down by Cooper Connolly on three before an optimistic drive off Beardman wound up in Josh Inglis’ gloves. The celebrations showed how much that wicket meant but he was just warming up. Jordan Cox followed to another defensive nick and Beardman showed his range by bouncing out Sam Curran , who hooked obligingly to fine leg for a seven-ball duck. Liam Dawson also fell without score, the fifth victim of a dream debut. Australia made easy work of their 131 chase (AP) England’s woes continued as Jamie Overton ’s ugly top-edge

Liam Dawson also fell without score, the fifth victim of a dream debut. Australia made easy work of their 131 chase (AP) England’s woes continued as Jamie Overton ’s ugly top-edge was plucked one-handed by the returning Johnson but Will Jacks ’ 25 and Atkinson’s punchy 29 not out saw them double their total. Beardman returned to end the innings, dismissing Jofra Archer to claim record debut figures for Australia and match England’s best ever analysis in the format, by Reece Topley in 2022. Atkinson bowled Head with his first delivery but Australia never threatened to let the result slip. Marsh put his foot down, blazing four sixes and four fours, effectively settling the matter by the time flicked Overton to deep-midwicket in the ninth over. Banton misjudged a steepling catch to spare Connolly on five, who added 22 more before poking Archer to gully. Inglis and Matt Renshaw did the rest with minimal fuss, leaving 159 deliveries unused.

item.title: Harry Kane breaks England appearance record and moves sixth for all-time international goals
item.description: Harry Kane breaks England appearance record and moves sixth for all-time international goals Harry Kane is now England 's most-capped men's player of all time after winning his 126th cap in a 2-1 Nations League victory over Croatia at Wembley. The England captain moves clear of goalkeeper Peter Shilton, whose 125 caps were won between 1970 and 1990. Kane had drawn level with Shilton last month, scoring twice as England beat the Czech Republic 3-0 at Wembley. The 33-year-old's record night arrives less than three weeks after he became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or. Ahead of the game, he spoke about his favourite England memories and named his 'biggest dream' as he chases major team trophies. A Wembley send-off fit for a record breaker Wembley marked the milestone before kick-off. A giant tifo of Kane was unfurled in the west stand, and the striker showed his Ballon d'Or trophy to the crowd. Shilton handed over a commemorative cap, Prince William presented a framed shirt and Croatia captain Luka Modric gave Kane a glass-encased football. It was a replica of the first ball the English took to Croatia in 1880. Kane also had a hand in the opening goal. Playing deeper in midfield, he slipped a diagonal pass through for Jude Bellingham down the right, and Bellingham cut it back for Morgan Rogers to score. The appearance record sits alongside the goalscoring one. Kane passed the old England mark of 53 goals in March 2023, and the Bayern Munich forward now has 92 international goals. He's now equal sixth for international goals in men's football , level with Robert Lewandowski. Romelu Lukaku (94) is the only active player ahead of Kane on the all-time list, after Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi's recent retirements. England play Spain in Madrid on Sunday, and a win would make Thomas Tuchel's side seeded for the Nations League quarter-finals at Easter, with the finals to follow next June.

item.title: Bears Stadium Bids Flood In As Developers Push City Plan
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Developers are flooding the market with unsolicited bids to keep the Chicago Bears in the city, but the team’s focus remains on a suburban deal or a move to Indiana. This bid arrives as the Bears prepare for a legislative session in Illinois starting Nov. 17, yet the franchise has not endorsed any of these urban proposals. The group plans to span about 100 acres and include a stadium for 75,000 fans alongside thousands of new homes. They argue that an urban site offers better economic value than remote suburbs. “It is our belief that a modern, competitive dome stadium such as the one that we are proposing will outperform suburban locations such as Arlington Heights or northwest Indiana,” said Quintin Primo III, founder and executive chairman of Capri Investment Group, during a news conference in Bronzeville, according to Yahoo . Local leaders back the idea, but the NFL has previously flagged the specific Reese parcel as too narrow with active rail lines running through it. City Dreams Versus Team Reality While local boosters push for a downtown solution, the Bears are actively exploring a path across the state line. Nearly nine months ago, Indiana state leaders approved a funding package, and due diligence has been completed regarding two potential locations in Hammond. The team has not commented on the specific Chicago proposals but is watching the Illinois political process closely. “We expect productive dialogue with both leadership teams in the coming weeks,” the Bears said last week regarding the two states, according to Yahoo Sports . The franchise is seeking property tax certainty and infrastructure help, with its main focus still on its own land in suburban Arlington Heights. Capri’s group is prepared to purchase the Bears’ current Arlington Heights property, which would solve the land issue but force the team to abandon its preferred suburban setup. Chicago 4th Ward Alderman Lamont Robinson voiced strong support for the Bronzeville plan, stating it serves the community best. “I believe with everything I have, it’s the right thing for the 4th ward. And the right thing for Chicago and the bears,” Robinson said. The developers claim their plan will shape the city for generations, but the team holds the real power in the negotiation. The Clock Ticks on Illinois Newly reelected Gov. JB Pritzker intends to advance a Bears-related bill during the upcoming veto session, creating a critical moment for the stadium saga. The recent rise in developer activity suggests growing confidence that a bill could pass, even as the team keeps its Indiana option alive. The Reese option joins similar unsolicited offers made in recent weeks for sites at the former South Works steel mill and Rate Field. “We have an opportunity to make a decision that will shape Chicago for generations,” said Quintin Primo III, Capri founder and executive chairman. item.title: Bloomington South girls basketball win over North completes county sweep
item.description: Just two weeks into the season and the Bloomington South girls basketball team has vanquished it's two county rivals. The annual meeting with Bloomington North was pushed up a month earlier than in the past, with the Cougars needing to adjust their schedule as new members of the Mid-State Conference. So it was a great early-season introduction to a sectional-like atmosphere for both teams in front of a vocal crowd at South on Thursday, Nov. 12. Offense was hard to come by as the Panthers held off a second-half rally by North, getting a huge 3-pointer from freshman Quinn Wurtzman with 2:10 left in a five-point game to pull out a 48-37 win. It followed a much less rowdy 62-20 rout of Edgewood on Tuesday. More: Senior seldomly comes off field for Bloomington South football "We knew it was going to be a great crowd," North coach Kiley Jarrett said. "That's what we wanted. We wanted to simulate a playoff atmosphere and that's what it was. "I just think we just got in too big of a hole in the first half. We fought like hell to get it back within five points and a just a couple possessions here and there that made the difference." Emotions were also running high with South junior transfer Kate Lehr playing her first game against her old mates. She came out fiery to score eight of her 12 points in the first period. From there, the offense spread out among the top eight, with six scoring with five points or more. "Playing them this early, I kind of figured it would be like that," South coach Larry Winters said. "I say it often, if they'd play with the same energy against us against other teams, they'd come out with the win. They came out, 1, because Kate's here but 2, because they always play us that way. "And tonight they did a really good job because they kept our two scorers from scoring." South finished 15-of-48 shooting, hitting 5 of 16 3-pointers but also going 13-of-15 at the line. "We were trying to score more than in any other game," Winters said. "We talked about that, let the shots find you, don't try to find the shots. Tonight, we tried to find the shots. But everybody wants to show out in front of every one, so that's what happens." Winters is confident the offense will get back on track since so many have been contributing so far. "They can all score and if you're sharing the ball, that's going to happen," Winters said. "Annika (Smith) was 1-for-10 and Tatum (DeVries) took three shots. There's going to be nights like that gives an opportunity for somebody else to step up and do something. "If teams want to concentrate on a couple players when you have as many as we do, then somebody just has to step up." The annual meeting with Bloomington North was pushed up a month earlier than in the past, with the Cougars needing to adjust their schedule as new members of the Mid-State Conference. We wanted to simulate a playoff atmosphere and that's what it was. "I just think we just got in too big of a hole in the first half. We fought like hell to get it back within five points and a just a couple possessions here and there that made the difference." Emotions were also running high with South junior transfer Kate Lehr playing her first game against her old mates. She came out fiery to score eight of her 12 points in the first period. From there, the offense spread out among the top eight, with six scoring with five points or more. "Playing them this early, I kind of figured it would be like that," South coach Larry Winters said. "I say it often, if they'd play with the same energy against us against other teams, they'd come out with the win. They came out, 1, because Kate's here but 2, because they always play us that way. "And tonight they did a really good job because they kept our two scorers from scoring." South finished 15-of-48 shooting, hitting 5 of 16 3-pointers but also going 13-of-15 at the line. "We were trying to score more than in any other game," Winters said. "We talked about that, let the shots find you, don't try to find the shots. Tonight, we tried to find the shots. But everybody wants to show out in front of every one, so that's what happens." Winters is confident the offense will get back on track since so many have been contributing so far. "They can all score and if you're sharing the ball, that's going to happen," Winters said. "Annika (Smith) was 1-for-10 and Tatum (DeVries) took three shots. There's going to be nights like that gives an opportunity for somebody else to step up and do something. "If teams want to concentrate on a couple players when you have as many as we do, then somebody just has to step up." North digs hole in first half South (2-1) will always lean on its defense, and forcing 11 turnovers in the first half led to some easy buckets and a 29-16 lead at the break. North had some key players in early foul trouble and the physical affects of the South press led to some 'tired' errors. "It was just mistakes on our part," Jarrett said. "Foul trouble didn't help us at all, it got us out of our typical rotation." But the Panthers' offensive struggles peaked in the third, going 2-of-11, forcing up some tough shots in the lane all night. That allowed the Cougars (0-2), who had just five more turnovers and played strong half-court defense most of the night, to chip away at the deficit. "We know that when we play them that if we can keep them in the half-court and not turn the ball over, then we're going to be in good shape," Jarrett said. North got within 33-27 at the end of three, but South wouldn't let them get any closer. A jump hook by Quinnly Fife and a banked in 3 by Avery Schwartzman from the top of the key while being fouled made it 38-29 with 6:26 to go. But a 3 from Rilynn Williams, who had a game high 13 points, made it 40-35 with 2:40 left. "She definitely is a more assertive player this year," Jarrett said. "And she stepped up tonight and made some huge plays for us. That 3 from the corner was absolutely huge. And I thought she did a good job defensively on Lehr." But that's when Wurtzman took the next big shot of the night, knocking home a 3 from 22 feet to start an 8-0 run that put the game away. "Knowing Quinn, she was ready for that shot and she'll be ready for that again," Jarrett said "It may say she's a freshman but she doesn't play like it and we knew that coming in. "Credit to her. That was a momentum changer because I definitely felt like momentum was on our side before that." All the same, Winters is looking at the big picture with his younger players. "That was a big 3 but there were three layups she missed," Winters said. "If you're going to make the long one, make the short one. But that's the pressure of playing in your first North-South game." More: 20 Bloomington area girls basketball returning players to watch in 2026-27 season Growing pains for Edgewood South started the week with a 62-20 win at Edgewood, a game that got away quickly after the young Mustangs tied it at 8-8 with 1:40 left in the first quarter. The Panthers scored the next 22 points as Edgewood coughed it up 20 times in the first half. It was 31-10 at the break and South put the running clock in motion late in the third, up 49-13. Edgewood was limited to four field goals, just one inside the arc. The frustration was evident, but South is also likely the best team the Mustangs will see all season. "You just have to harp on the positive things that we did," Edgewood coach Noah Stuckey said. "I feel like, that first quarter, we competed as well as we possibly could. We handled their physicality and got to the free throw line and then we just kinds of wore down. "We got punched and wilted a little bit and didn't bring the energy in the second half." It was just the second varsity team for the entire lineup so the speed and strength it takes to succeed at that level was on display. On either side of that loss against the best team on their schedule, the Mustangs opened with a win over Greencastle 42-32 and then topped South Putnam 40-31 on Thursday. "It felt awkward," Stuckey said of the win over Greencastle. "We started very strong, we got in some foul trouble and they made a run at us. Then, the second half, Kaitlyn (Ripley) took over. She didn't play the second quarter and had 23 points. "The way they've been playing maybe the last couple of years is just stand and watch her," Stuckey said. "And we just can't rely on her to do everything. We've got to help her out and we kind of got in that run in the second and third quarter (against South)." item.title: Coldwater's Delaney leads 2026 Battle Creek Enquirer All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team
item.description: BATTLE CREEK - Never losing a game from late August until October. Winning a conference title and a district crown. For helping his team accomplish all of that, Coldwater's Ken Delaney is the 2026 All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team Coach of the Year. The All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team is selected by nominations from the city and area coaches and voted on by the Enquirer sports staff. MORE: Player capsules for the Battle Creek Enquirer All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team In his 18th season as head coach, Delaney is on a roll with state-ranked teams in back-to-back years as the Cardinals were 15-2-2 overall. Coldwater finished as Interstate 8 Conference champs with a 6-0 record in the league and won a second district title in the last three years. Along the way, Coldwater went unbeaten from August 20 until the regionals and climbed to as high as No. 12 in the Michigan Interscholastic High School Soccer Coaches rankings in Division 2. Delaney is joined on the All-Enquirer team by Cardinals players Abdulhamid Munassar, Ahmen Norman, Riath Shamaala and Jensely Norvilus. Lakeview finished as All-City Tournament champs and adds Mang Sung, Richard Lian and Cristian Duran to the team. Harper Creek had the most wins in program history as Beavers' Jake Cushman, Broderick Hanger and TJ Ruble were named All-Enquirer. Also from the city, earning All-Enquirer honors, are Pennfield's Philipp Kruetz and Everett Wilkins, Battle Creek Central's Yoani Bautista Trejo and Deangelo Crape, with the St. Philip/Calhoun co-op program adding Ashton Heighton and Ben Kaczanowski. Among area teams, Marshall's Brandon Baker, Rowdy Joseph, Carson Clapper and Trenton Wolkiewicz were named as All-Enquirer members, as well as Gull Lake's Charlie Trantham, Ethan Waldorf. Bill Broderick can be reached at bbroderi@battlecreekenquirer.com. Follow him on X /Twitter: @billbroderick This article originally appeared on Battle Creek Enquirer: Coldwater's Delaney leads 2026 Battle Creek Enquirer All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team

item.title: Legendary coach Terry Waters finds new role at Fishburne
item.description: WAYNESBORO — Terry Waters is a legendary wrestling coach in the area. He was inducted into the Virginia Chapter of the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2022, and his photo and biographical info are in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in Stillwater, Oklahoma. Most assumed he would coach wrestling until he retired and then just walk away. Raised in a hot bed of wrestling in Pennsylvania, Waters was a student at Milton Hershey School, a boarding school for low-income families in Hershey. He and his brother were among the first Black students at the school after it integrated. Locally, Waters has coached at Staunton, Riverheads and Fort Defiance high schools, as well as at Washington & Lee University, where he was an assistant. He came to Fishburne in 2015. This past summer, he announced he was retiring from coaching. It seemed to be the end of an amazing career, but then he announced, not too longer afterward, that he would be staying at the Waynesboro school to serve as athletic director. He's now through the fall season and about to start winter sports. "It hasn't gone totally smooth, but it's been a great transition," Waters said. "The thing is I still get to coordinate a lot with the kids. That was the big decision for me, how much involvement would I get to have with the kids." He is now dealing with 20 or so coaches, not just his own assistants like he did as wrestling coach. That has been challenging. "You're dealing with 20, 24 personalities," he said. "That becomes a situation where you have to take a step back and try to understand each coach individually." Coaching for 49 years, Waters feels he had a great relationship with most of his athletic directors. He has tried to take lessons he learned from them into this job. He learned what kind of athletic director he wanted to be and what kind he didn't want to be. "I wanted to be fair, and I believe that I'm open and positive if a coach wants to talk with me," he said. "Obviously taking over a new position, you want to change some things — your approach and things like that — but overall it's gone pretty well." Fishburne offers 10 sports. Asked if he ever thought about being an athletic director, Waters took a long pause before answering. He said maybe it was in the back of his mind, but it was never something he really pursued. "When this happened, I really think it was God opening the door," Waters said. "This situation just came open." Every year, at least in recent years, someone would ask the veteran coach how much longer. His answer was always one more year. He'd talk with his wife about his future in coaching after the season ended. She would tell him if he still had the energy and the desire, he should keep coaching. "My brother pretty much summed it up when he told me if you like what you're doing, there is no sense in retiring," he said. But this summer, he clearly remembers waking up one morning and thinking, "I'm done." He told the Fishburne staff about his decision. He was planning to just walk away, but then the athletic director position opened. Waters decided to apply. "I've had athletic directors across the state send me notes telling me if I needed any help just let them know," Waters said. He said Frank Kahrs at Grace Christian has been particularly helpful. He's also talked with Staunton's David Tibbs about some questions he had. All the connections Waters has built over the years are proving to be helpful in the new job. "I believe I'm here because it's where God wants me," Waters said. The day-to-day life of an athletics director is never the same, and never boring, Waters said. "You spend a lot more time than I actually though on the computer," he said, "sending emails out, setting schedules, things like that." It's about a 10-hour a day job, give or take, and Waters said he's fine with that. He does have two assistant athletic directors that help take some of the burden off of him, but Waters said he'll be at every home event at Fishburne. He feels it's his responsibility. "I love what I do," he said. Wrestling this winter may be the toughest for him because he's not coaching — although, maybe not. "I don't think I'm going to miss it as much as other people think I'm going to miss it," Waters said. "I just want to make sure I don't step on toes." Rick Palmer is taking over as head wrestling coach at Fishburne. Waters said he has confidence in Palmer's abilities to continue leading the program. Still, Waters said home wrestling events will be difficult, sitting in the stands watching instead of in the corner of the mat coaching. "That is something that will be hard," he said, "but I'm prepared for that. I've done all I want to do in coaching in 49 years. I don't have anything else to prove. I was ready to step down. I was comfortable in my decision." More: 'Last ride' for Wilson Memorial star Bree Kindig More: Tyree Scott takes Rollos BBQ from food truck to Craigsville shop Patrick Hite is a reporter at The News Leader. Cummins hit out at Khawaja for claiming that all the players, including the bowlers, knew about the use of sandpaper in 2018. Cummins reiterated the bowlers' statement from 2021. Pat Cummins responds to Khawaja's allegations about Sandpapergate in media interaction On Friday morning, Australia's Test and ODI captain Pat Cummins finally addressed the controversy that has rocked Australian cricket in the last one week. The infamous 'Sandpapergate' from 2018 made the headlines once again after former national team opener Usman Khawaja made explosive claims about the incident during Australia's tour of South Africa eight years ago. All three players had to serve lengthy bans, while Smith and Warner lost their captaincy and vice-captaincy, respectively. Pat Cummins responds to Khawaja's allegations about Sandpapergate in media interaction On Friday morning, Australia's Test and ODI captain Pat Cummins finally addressed the controversy that has rocked Australian cricket in the last one week. The infamous 'Sandpapergate' from 2018 made the headlines once again after former national team opener Usman Khawaja made explosive claims about the incident during Australia's tour of South Africa eight years ago. In his recently released autobiography, 'Sabr' , Khawaja claimed that the entire Australian team from the 2018 South Africa tour was aware of the use of sandpaper in Cape Town and not just the three players - David Warner, Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft - who were implicated. The official line from Cricket Australia, however, since the incident in Cape Town, has held that only Smith, Warner and Bancroft had knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball during the third Test against South Africa. All three players had to serve lengthy bans, while Smith and Warner lost their captaincy and vice-captaincy, respectively. Days after Khawaja's explosive claim, the current captain, Cummins, who was also an integral part of the Australian side from 2018, addressed the media to clarify his stance on the incident . MORE: McGrath claims only those with 'agendas' want to keep talking about Sandpapergate Cummins told reporters, "When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, that is 100% wrong. I've said that consistently for the last eight years, I did not know that was happening." The fast bowler added, "But I think Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that. He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense. I was genuinely shocked this week when I found out that Usman admitted that he told Cam [Bancroft] to be careful when using sandpaper. "That's not the Usman that I know. It's not the Usman that I think, or that has been part of a team that's helped rebuild this Australian cricket culture over the last eight years, and you know the Usman that would have stopped that from happening there and then. Usman's a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations." While Cummins was in favour of Khawaja expressing his opinion freely, he also refuted the claims of the batter. He said, "In his book, Ussie has been casual with my life and the lives of many others, and I think Australian cricket. I support his right to tell a story 100%. I'm really glad that he feels like he can, but we have to be accountable for the things that we say and do. "There was no master plan around using illegal methods. I think that's maybe something that hasn't been spoken about enough. People assume you've gone from very legal methods (to get it the ball to reverse) to suddenly taking sandpaper, and there must have been some huge master plan. The truth, that is not the case. That's one of the reasons why I really want to talk through this, because context and details matter around this. There's no grand plan. There's no team meeting. There's no bowlers saying this is what must happen. I think there are natural progressions that get you there." MORE: Late Shane Warne's Sandpapergate questions to CA and 'bowling cartel' resurface Becky Cummins salutes husband Pat's strength after the brave media interaction Cummins' press conference divided opinions in Australian cricket. His former teammate, Warner, who served a ban for the Sandpapergate, slammed the pace bowler and reiterated his support for Khawaj a. The Australian captain, though, found support in his wife, Becky, who made a social media post to salute her husband's courage for showing up in front of the media, amid the crisis. On her Instagram story, Beck wrote, "Once again, I am beyond proud and blown away by this man's strength and leadership. This is why I married you." Becky Cummins latest instagram story " Once again, I am beyond proud and blown away by this man's strength and leadership. " "That's why I married you". https://t.co/cwA6PiwLI9 — Sunrisers Army (@srhorangearmy) November 13, 2026 MORE: 'Tried eradicating it': Cummins admits Australia of 2018 had a 'win at all costs' mentality Sandpapergate is far from over Warner’s decision to speak openly about Cummins tells us that the wounds from Cape Town haven’t healed. Two players who shared a dressing room for years are now giving opposite accounts of the same match, and both are sure that they are right. That alone makes it hard for the sport to follow Waugh’s advice and simply move on. His point that nobody from that dressing room, besides the three punished players, reached out in eight years is a powerful one, and it speaks to the 'mateship' that Australian cricket likes to talk about. The human cost he described, including the loss that he and his wife suffered, also deserves respect. What the episode needs now is clarity rather than more noise. If Warner tells his own story in a book, it may finally give the public something solid to judge, though it will also keep the saga alive for longer. item.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
item.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. The wobbly Nigerian economy doesn’t help matters either, as people are putting off marriage till they can grow their finances, leading to advanced marital age across both genders. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate. item.dc:creator: Uwaezu Kanu
item.content:encoded: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. The wobbly Nigerian economy doesn’t help matters either, as people are putting off marriage till they can grow their finances, leading to advanced marital age across both genders. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate. On the village aspect, families now live further apart than ever before thanks to japa, and even those within Nigeria struggle to come together for various reasons, one of which is high transportation costs. While there are certainly challenges, becoming a mother at an older age can also have its advantages. You tend to be more mature, grounded in your identity, and confident in your choices. You have a clear understanding of the kind of child or children you wish to raise and are intentional in selecting a partner who aligns well with your values. Additionally, because you have prioritised building wealth, you have more resources at your disposal, which can significantly enhance the comfort of both you and your child. This financial stability helps you avoid being in survival mode, allowing you to approach motherhood with greater calmness. Research shows that well-regulated mothers often raise emotionally balanced children. You also have the means to hire highly qualified staff from reputable nanny agencies to assist in caring for your child. One potential advantage—or disadvantage, depending on your perspective—of becoming pregnant at age 35 or older is the increased likelihood of having twins. As women approach menopause, natural biological changes in hormone levels can raise the chances of conceiving non-identical (fraternal or dizygotic) twins. This could be exciting if you have a preference for twins, but it may be something to consider carefully if you do not. There are several ways to ensure that age doesn’t truncate your dreams of motherhood. The most important one is taking care of your mind and your body. Exercise, eat a balanced diet, and prioritise protein and fibre. Schedule yearly check-ins with your OB-GYN to check your overall health, among other things. Take your vitamins seriously, especially folic acid. Try to avoid added sugar as much as you can. Get at least 8 hours of sleep every day. Most importantly, do not give in to the fear-mongering online. Women age 35 and above can and do get pregnant without any medical interventions, going on to have healthy babies. And even if you end up needing medical intervention, it is nothing to be ashamed of. Finally, while you wait to start your own family, go out, have fun, travel the world if you can afford to, and live your life to the fullest. Trust me, I know what it’s like. *** Featured Image by Cottonbro for Pexels. The post Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: 5 Android phones just as powerful as the iPhone 18 Pro Max in 2026
item.description: Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Max is one of the most powerful smartphones available in 2026, but it faces stiff competition from Android manufacturers investing heavily in mobile processing, artificial intelligence, gaming and camera technology. Powered by Apple’s new A20 Pro chip, the iPhone 18 Pro Max delivers improved CPU and graphics performance, alongside enhanced capabilities for running demanding applications and AI-powered features. Apple says the processor delivers up to 40 per cent faster graphics performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. Apple. However, Android manufacturers have also introduced flagship devices powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and newer Extreme Gen 6 processors, as well as MediaTek’s Dimensity 9600 series. These processors bring substantial improvements in computing power, graphics rendering, multitasking and energy efficiency, allowing selected Android smartphones to compete with Apple’s latest flagship. Here are five Android smartphones that offer comparable flagship-level performance to the iPhone 18 Pro Max in 2026. 1. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is arguably one of the strongest Android alternatives to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, particularly for users who want a combination of processing power, advanced photography and artificial intelligence features. The smartphone is powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy processor, a customised chipset designed to deliver improved CPU, graphics and AI performance. According to Samsung, the processor provides a 39 per cent improvement in neural processing unit performance, supporting faster AI operations and more efficient multitasking. The Galaxy S26 Ultra also features a 6.9-inch display, a 200-megapixel main camera, an improved cooling system and an integrated S Pen. Its combination of high-end hardware, Galaxy AI features and advanced camera capabilities makes it a strong competitor to Apple’s premium smartphone. Samsung has also committed to seven years of software updates, giving the device a longer support lifespan. Android Authority+1 2. OnePlus 15 The OnePlus 15 is another Android flagship capable of competing with Apple’s latest smartphone, particularly in gaming and demanding everyday tasks. It runs on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor, featuring the company’s Oryon CPU and Adreno 840 graphics processor. The device comes with up to 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, providing sufficient memory and storage capacity for demanding applications, multitasking and mobile gaming. OnePlus has also equipped the smartphone with a 6.78-inch display supporting refresh rates of up to 165Hz in compatible games. Its 7,300mAh battery, 120W wired charging and 50W wireless charging further strengthen its appeal to users who spend considerable time gaming, streaming and working on their smartphones. item.title: US lawmakers summon Nvidia ex-CEO after affair with suspected spy
item.description: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters. “Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology,” Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote Thursday on X. Scott said he was requesting Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs. It joins a call for a closed-door interview with the leather-jacketed, 63-year-old Huang on December 1 by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena. Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. While Nvidia’s board searches for a permanent successor to Huang, who spent 33 years at the helm of the firm he co-founded, chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO. Nvidia hit gold when the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in 2022 sparked a global rush to develop AI, with its processors — once designed for video game graphics — becoming a crucial ingredient to train and run the technology. – Informal Trump adviser – Nvidia did not give a reason for the departure of Huang, who also gave up his board seat. Huang is Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6 percent, according to the company. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI, and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives called it “a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry”. But he said the board had done what it needed: “rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him.” The board named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as chair, and said it expected the company’s operations and product roadmap “to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companies including Cisco and Microsoft. Nvidia hit gold when the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in 2022 sparked a global rush to develop AI, with its processors — once designed for video game graphics — becoming a crucial ingredient to train and run the technology. – Informal Trump adviser – Nvidia did not give a reason for the departure of Huang, who also gave up his board seat. Huang is Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6 percent, according to the company. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI, and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives called it “a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry”. But he said the board had done what it needed: “rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him.” The board named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as chair, and said it expected the company’s operations and product roadmap “to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companies including Cisco and Microsoft. Trump, who had stood by Huang throughout the scandal, said former Apple boss Tim Cook should take over. “A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump said on his Truth Social network, adding that Cook had made Apple “one of the great companies of the world at a fairly short range”. – ‘Going through hell’ – Singapore said Thursday it had barred Alice Huang, a Chinese national, from re-entering the country in February for giving investigators inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed, though she was not investigated for espionage. Nvidia’s board opened a probe on Sunday into reporting that Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort,” while saying it retained confidence in him. When asked Thursday if Jensen should have stepped down, Trump said it would depend. “If the woman was a spy, yes. If the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different,” Trump said in an interview. But Trump said he was confident that Huang will “end up on his feet,” adding: “I spoke to him yesterday. He’s going through hell. What he feels most badly about is his wife and family.” At the heart of the spy allegations is the race between the United States and China for supremacy in an industry widely seen as the next industrial revolution. Key US lawmakers, including Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, called Thursday for answers on what the Trump administration knew about Huang’s ties to a suspected Chinese spy, days before Trump travels to China for a summit. Reports allege the Commerce Department under Secretary Howard Lutnick may have failed to act on suspicions that Megaspeed was helping reroute restricted Nvidia technology to China. Singapore’s home ministry said it had repeatedly sought information from the US Justice Department and FBI on a US server supplier during its Megaspeed probe, but “received limited information or assistance.” On Thursday, Malaysia also said Friday it was investigating a subsidiary of Megaspeed International over the possible diversion of advanced AI chips to other countries. The post US lawmakers summon Nvidia ex-CEO after affair with suspected spy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: [2027] NASS condemns electoral violence nationwide
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with the National Assembly condemning nationwide violence linked to the 2027 general elections. Another headline features President Bola Tinubu begging voters in Edo State during a campaign rally to re-elect him so he could complete ongoing projects. Vanguard also reports that ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has begun deploying non-sensitive materials nationwide. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian reports that violence threatens credible polls in 2027 as the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) trade blame over an attack during a town hall meeting organised for NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Lagos. The Punch leads with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) fixing November 28, 2026, for a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise ahead of the 2027 general elections to test upgrades to its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and electronic results transmission. Lastly, Daily Trust reports that bread makers have lamented the high cost of borrowing and rising operating expenses, warning that the combination of expensive credit, energy costs and increasing prices of production inputs is threatening the survival of bakeries across the country. Vanguard News The post Nigerian newspapers review: [2027] NASS condemns electoral violence nationwide appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Abductors of FUNAAB graduate, three others demand N500m ransom
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The abductors of a recent graduate of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), Adedoja Hannah, and three other individuals have reportedly demanded a ransom of N500 million for their release. The victims were allegedly kidnapped on Tuesday night when suspected gunmen invaded a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta, Ogun State, where they were working. The development was disclosed by the Students’ Union Government (SUG) of FUNAAB in a statement posted on its official Facebook platform on Thursday, expressing concern over the safety of the victims and appealing to members of the university community and the general public to remain calm. According to the union, Hannah, a recent graduate of the Department of Agricultural Administration, was among the four people abducted during the incident. Providing an account of the circumstances surrounding her disappearance, the union stated that Hannah was last seen on Monday, while her telephone has remained unreachable since the reported abduction. The statement partly reads, “The Students’ Union Government wishes to update the FUNAAB community and the general public on the abduction of Adedoja Hannah, a recent graduate of the Department of Agricultural Administration, Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), alongside three other individuals at a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta. “According to information received, the incident occurred on Tuesday night when suspected kidnappers reportedly invaded the farm where the victims were working. This development has understandably heightened concerns over their safety and the circumstances surrounding the incident. “The incident was reported to the appropriate security authorities, and the police have been working on the matter since Tuesday. The development was disclosed by the Students’ Union Government (SUG) of FUNAAB in a statement posted on its official Facebook platform on Thursday, expressing concern over the safety of the victims and appealing to members of the university community and the general public to remain calm. According to the union, Hannah, a recent graduate of the Department of Agricultural Administration, was among the four people abducted during the incident. Providing an account of the circumstances surrounding her disappearance, the union stated that Hannah was last seen on Monday, while her telephone has remained unreachable since the reported abduction. The statement partly reads, “The Students’ Union Government wishes to update the FUNAAB community and the general public on the abduction of Adedoja Hannah, a recent graduate of the Department of Agricultural Administration, Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), alongside three other individuals at a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta. “According to information received, the incident occurred on Tuesday night when suspected kidnappers reportedly invaded the farm where the victims were working. Hannah was last seen on Monday, and her phone has remained unreachable since the incident. “Further information indicates that the abductors have demanded a ransom of ₦500 million for the release of all four victims. This development has understandably heightened concerns over their safety and the circumstances surrounding the incident. “The incident was reported to the appropriate security authorities, and the police have been working on the matter since Tuesday. Security efforts are ongoing, with attention directed towards locating the victims and securing their safe release. “We understand the concern this incident has generated, particularly among residents and members of the university community around the Alabata axis. However, we appeal to everyone to remain calm and allow the relevant authorities to carry out their investigations and response. “It is equally important that information shared publicly is accurate and responsible. Unverified reports and speculation should be avoided, especially where they could interfere with ongoing security efforts. “The Union is deeply concerned about the safety of Hannah and the other victims. When contacted, the Ogun State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, confirmed the abduction. Babaseyi said, “we are on the issue since it happened; rescue operations are in top gear”. The post Abductors of FUNAAB graduate, three others demand N500m ransom appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Years of injustice’ fuel northern Nigeria violence, says bandit leader
item.description: Decades of discrimination and extortion against Fulani herders are stoking the growing violence in northern Nigeria — unrest which will only swell until authorities tame the rampant corruption in the region, a bandit kingpin told AFP in a rare interview. Northwest and central Nigeria have for years been terrorised by gangs known locally as “bandits”, who raid villages, rustle cattle, conduct kidnappings and impose “taxes” on farmers and miners. The interview with one such gang leader came during the reporting of an article for The New York Review of Books, in a piece published Thursday, co-authored by an American academic and writer Helen Epstein and AFP northern Nigeria reporter Aminu Abubakar. “Years of injustices are what pushed Fulani herders into banditry. We were never criminals before,” a bandit leader named Babangida said. Banditry traces its roots to conflicts between herders and farmers over access to limited land and water, made worse by climate change and population growth. Out of the violence emerged powerful gangs, largely composed of Fulani herders. The conflict has spiralled from raids and revenge attacks into broader, complex criminality by gangs numbering from around a dozen to well into the hundreds. They have created a kidnapping economy that raises hundreds of thousands of dollars, and at times entered alliances with Nigerian jihadists. After months of negotiation, Babangida agreed to an interview in a remote Katsina state village, following the intervention of a former government peace negotiator. “Justice is the only way out. When justice is upheld, everyone will live in peace,” said the bandit, who asked only to be identified by his first name. In the meantime, violence reigns: last week, in neighbouring Zamfara state, bandits set fire to a home during a raid, killing a family of 12. Earlier this month, gunmen killed eight police officers, and in September, more than 80 people, mostly women, were kidnapped in Zamfara and Niger states — many while working their fields. Worsening insecurity has become a major issue in the ongoing presidential campaign, as Bola Tinubu runs for a second term in January polls. – Corruption – Clad in a blue kaftan, the 38-year-old passes for a normal villager, save for the Kalashnikov rifle in his hand. “No bandit just picked up a gun overnight and turned to violence. There is always a story behind it,” said Babangida, sheltering from the scorching heat under a neem tree. He described the raid as based on indiscriminate suspicions that all Fulani are bandits. He was forced to pay millions of naira (thousands of dollars) to post bail for his mother and brother. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: Decades of discrimination and extortion against Fulani herders are stoking the growing violence in northern Nigeria — unrest which will only swell until authorities tame the rampant corruption in the region, a bandit kingpin told AFP in a rare interview. Northwest and central Nigeria have for years been terrorised by gangs known locally as “bandits”, who raid villages, rustle cattle, conduct kidnappings and impose “taxes” on farmers and miners. The interview with one such gang leader came during the reporting of an article for The New York Review of Books, in a piece published Thursday, co-authored by an American academic and writer Helen Epstein and AFP northern Nigeria reporter Aminu Abubakar. “Years of injustices are what pushed Fulani herders into banditry. We were never criminals before,” a bandit leader named Babangida said. Banditry traces its roots to conflicts between herders and farmers over access to limited land and water, made worse by climate change and population growth. Out of the violence emerged powerful gangs, largely composed of Fulani herders. The conflict has spiralled from raids and revenge attacks into broader, complex criminality by gangs numbering from around a dozen to well into the hundreds. They have created a kidnapping economy that raises hundreds of thousands of dollars, and at times entered alliances with Nigerian jihadists. After months of negotiation, Babangida agreed to an interview in a remote Katsina state village, following the intervention of a former government peace negotiator. “Justice is the only way out. When justice is upheld, everyone will live in peace,” said the bandit, who asked only to be identified by his first name. In the meantime, violence reigns: last week, in neighbouring Zamfara state, bandits set fire to a home during a raid, killing a family of 12. Earlier this month, gunmen killed eight police officers, and in September, more than 80 people, mostly women, were kidnapped in Zamfara and Niger states — many while working their fields. Worsening insecurity has become a major issue in the ongoing presidential campaign, as Bola Tinubu runs for a second term in January polls. – Corruption – Clad in a blue kaftan, the 38-year-old passes for a normal villager, save for the Kalashnikov rifle in his hand. “No bandit just picked up a gun overnight and turned to violence. There is always a story behind it,” said Babangida, sheltering from the scorching heat under a neem tree. Babangida said he turned to banditry a decade ago after his family’s 97 cows were seized by a team of police and vigilantes. He described the raid as based on indiscriminate suspicions that all Fulani are bandits. He was forced to pay millions of naira (thousands of dollars) to post bail for his mother and brother. He only recovered 10 cattle, which he used “to buy guns, one of which I’m holding now” and moved his family to a camp in the bush. Fulani herders have for generations practiced semi-nomadic herding, moving from the arid north in the dry season to the more fertile Middle Belt and southern regions, through long-established grazing routes. Desertification caused by overgrazing, the expansion of farms, climate change, population growth, and the chopping down of forests for firewood have pushed farmers and herders into contact — including instances where herds move through farmland, eating crops and destroying fields. Meanwhile, local officials, including village chiefs, police, and the military, have done little to stop farmers from encroaching into grazing areas — and in some cases, colluded with them. – Discrimination – Both farmers and herders have suffered, with attacks on farming settlements sometimes leaving scores dead. Fulanis say they face marginalisation and discrimination at the hands of the government and security forces. When cows damage fields, “the village chief will set the fine well beyond the value of the crops destroyed,” Babangida said. “But when a farmer kills a herder’s cattle, it is declared the herder’s fault and he receives no compensation,” he added. “If the chief calls the police, they will connive with a judge to raise the fine even more.” – ‘He’s right’ – The Nigerian military routinely refers to bandits as “terrorists”, and runs a dedicated military campaign in the northwest to combat them. But, addressing Babangida’s claims of “injustice”, the Katsina state internal security commissioner told AFP: “He’s right… You can’t divorce that factor (from the) drivers of this criminality”. Nasiru Muazu told AFP his state has made efforts to initiate peace dialogues and solve underlying issues driving criminality, arguing “what is happening here in the northwest is a community-driven crisis,” unlike the jihadist conflict in northeast Nigeria. “It is a serious problem” trying to balance a firm response from security forces and local diplomacy, he added. – ‘Money’ and ‘revenge’ – Some bandit gangs, driven by economic motivations in the impoverished countryside, have become massive concerns, imposing “taxes” on farmers in areas all but abandoned by the state. The military often turns to air strikes to try to rein in bandit groups in areas outside its control. Vigilante groups — repeatedly accused of extra-judicial killings by herders — have formed among farmers. Peace deals have been repeatedly struck, only to collapse. Violence has swelled in recent years. – New generation – But even Babangida is worried about the change among his criminal circle, as older bandits are replaced by a younger — and more violent, he said — generation. He blamed young bandits — often under the influence of drugs, he said — for indiscriminate violence, including killing captives after ransoms were paid. Analysts have expressed concern over alliances between bandits, who have no ideological leaning, with Nigerian jihadists. Babangida admitted that some bandits align with jihadists for strategic reasons, but maintained that for most of his comrades “it is all about making money — and revenge.” The post ‘Years of injustice’ fuel northern Nigeria violence, says bandit leader appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC warns Okada riders against political violence in Oyo
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators in Oyo State against allowing politicians to use them as instruments of violence, thuggery and electoral malpractice ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission urged members of transport unions to resist attempts to involve them in activities capable of undermining public peace and the credibility of the electoral process before, during and after the elections. The Oyo State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Adeniran Tella, gave the warning on Thursday at the 2026 Day celebration of the Amalgamated Commercial Tricycle and Motorcycle Owners, Repairs and Riders Association of Nigeria (ACOMORAN), held alongside the launch of a book authored by the union’s chairman, Solomon Olugbode, at the Obafemi Awolowo Stadium, Oke-Ado, Ibadan. Tella, who was represented by the Head of INEC’s Information Unit, Olayiwola Awolowo, also urged members of the association to encourage their passengers and other members of the public to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). He stressed the importance of civic participation in the electoral process, saying commercial transport operators had a responsibility to protect democracy rather than allow themselves to be recruited into activities capable of threatening national security. “Let me be clear, do not allow yourselves to be used as instruments of violence or thuggery. The Nigeria Police Force has warned that the law will take its full course against anyone, no matter their status, who threatens public peace or engages in criminal conduct before, during or after the elections,” he said. Specifically, he charged ACOMORAN members to shun political violence, warning them against transporting weapons, money for vote-buying or individuals intending to disrupt the elections. “Your motorcycle or tricycle is a tool of livelihood, not a weapon of destruction. I urge you to remain politically neutral as a union,” he added. The INEC representative also cautioned the association against allowing its structures and operational resources to be deployed in support of any political party, noting that members retained the right to support candidates of their choice in their individual capacities. “While you have the right to support any candidate of your choice as individuals, the union’s infrastructure must never be hijacked to favour one party over another,” he said. He urged the transport operators to support INEC’s election logistics by ensuring the timely and safe movement of electoral materials and personnel whenever engaged by the commission. He also called on members to serve as voter education ambassadors by promoting peace, tolerance and responsible voting at motor parks and among their passengers. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators in Oyo State against allowing politicians to use them as instruments of violence, thuggery and electoral malpractice ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission urged members of transport unions to resist attempts to involve them in activities capable of undermining public peace and the credibility of the electoral process before, during and after the elections. The Oyo State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Adeniran Tella, gave the warning on Thursday at the 2026 Day celebration of the Amalgamated Commercial Tricycle and Motorcycle Owners, Repairs and Riders Association of Nigeria (ACOMORAN), held alongside the launch of a book authored by the union’s chairman, Solomon Olugbode, at the Obafemi Awolowo Stadium, Oke-Ado, Ibadan. Tella, who was represented by the Head of INEC’s Information Unit, Olayiwola Awolowo, also urged members of the association to encourage their passengers and other members of the public to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). He stressed the importance of civic participation in the electoral process, saying commercial transport operators had a responsibility to protect democracy rather than allow themselves to be recruited into activities capable of threatening national security. “Let me be clear, do not allow yourselves to be used as instruments of violence or thuggery. The Nigeria Police Force has warned that the law will take its full course against anyone, no matter their status, who threatens public peace or engages in criminal conduct before, during or after the elections,” he said. Specifically, he charged ACOMORAN members to shun political violence, warning them against transporting weapons, money for vote-buying or individuals intending to disrupt the elections. “Your motorcycle or tricycle is a tool of livelihood, not a weapon of destruction. I urge you to remain politically neutral as a union,” he added. The INEC representative also cautioned the association against allowing its structures and operational resources to be deployed in support of any political party, noting that members retained the right to support candidates of their choice in their individual capacities. “While you have the right to support any candidate of your choice as individuals, the union’s infrastructure must never be hijacked to favour one party over another,” he said. He urged the transport operators to support INEC’s election logistics by ensuring the timely and safe movement of electoral materials and personnel whenever engaged by the commission. He also called on members to serve as voter education ambassadors by promoting peace, tolerance and responsible voting at motor parks and among their passengers. Similarly, the Oyo State Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Abimbola, urged commercial transport operators to embrace peaceful conduct, describing their professionalism as critical to safer roads, efficient transportation and economic growth. Abimbola, who was represented by the Officer-in-Charge of the Motor Traffic Department of the state Police Command, Chief Superintendent of Police Lawrence Kehinde, described transport operators as important stakeholders in maintaining peace and security across the state. “Peace on our roads begins with the transporter. If commercial transporters conduct themselves peacefully, our cities will be safer, our journeys will be smoother, and our economy will grow,” he said. He added that peaceful conduct was a mark of professionalism, maturity and responsibility, urging every transporter to see himself as an ambassador of peace. The police commissioner also cautioned ACOMORAN members against violence and actions capable of disrupting public order during the 2027 elections. In his remarks, a leader of the Odua People’s Congress, Adesina Akinpelu, warned the transport operators against allowing politicians or other individuals to use them to foment trouble in the state. Akinpelu commended the commercial motorcyclists for sustaining their businesses despite prevailing economic difficulties, describing their services as indispensable to millions of Nigerians who depend on them for daily transportation. “Do not be used to cause troubles. Don’t let them use you. I salute your courage in this present economy. You provide essential transportation services to millions of Nigerians. Without you, many people cannot get to their destinations,” he said. He noted that the operators played important roles in the daily activities of market women, traders, students and other members of the public. Also speaking, a Muslim cleric, Mahmud Eleshinmeta, advised members of the association to exercise discipline in their personal lives, particularly in the use of their bodies, time and financial resources. He warned against substance abuse, stressing that success and the ability to perform their duties did not depend on consuming alcohol, drugs or other intoxicating substances. The cleric urged them to spend their resources prudently and adopt responsible lifestyles. Earlier, the Oyo State Chairman of ACOMORAN, Solomon Olugbode, said the 2026 Day celebration was organised to promote discipline, responsible conduct and professionalism among members. He said the event was also designed to sensitise members to the dangers of social vices and practices capable of undermining their personal lives and the reputation of the association. According to him, the association considered it necessary to use the occasion to engage members on issues beyond their daily commercial activities, including responsible citizenship, peaceful coexistence, personal development and their contributions to society. Olugbode said commercial transport operators had important responsibilities and must conduct themselves in ways that promote peace, safety and mutual respect. He further stressed the importance of continuous education and enlightenment, noting that the association’s development depended on members’ commitment to discipline, unity and adherence to the law. The chairman appreciated the dignitaries, security agencies, government representatives and other stakeholders who attended the celebration, urging members to translate the messages delivered at the event into positive actions.
